Applied both in the acquisition simulator setup dialog: a collapsible **Kinetics** panel with `k_rad`/`k_nrad` rate matrices that resize when the **Species** count changes (`n_species` field `call="species_changed"` → refresh), and the bottom `🛠 Tools` menu (Decay / Load / Save / View JSON). The per-species **Decay** modal now edits **amplitude + lifetime** pairs (was lifetime-only) — `_species_decay` accepts `[amp, τ]` pairs (or bare τ) and feeds `synthetic_decay(taus, amplitudes=amps)`. Tests: `test/gui/test_rate_matrix.py` (2, general) + acq `core/test/test_setup_widgets.py` (kinetics-tracks-species, amp/τ round-trip). See [subsystems/gui-autoform.md](/subsystems/gui-autoform.md).

## 2026-07-18
* **Acquisition simulator settings: a modal Decay editor (with load-existing-pattern) + compact Channels table.** The simulation setup dialog (`plugins/core/acq/tcspc_devices/simulation/setup_dialog.py`) had no way to define the fluorescence decay. New modal `DecaySettingsDialog` (opened by a `🧬 Decay…` button): a per-species lifetime (τ) table + Add/Remove, a shared Gaussian IRF FWHM, a `📂 Load pattern…` button to use an existing measured/saved decay histogram (text/.npy) instead of lifetimes, and a live decay preview (built through the canonical `synthetic_decay`). It writes back per-species `decay_lifetimes` / `decay_pattern_files` / `irf_fwhm_ns`, which `to_parameters` now emits and `build_engine` consumes (a loaded pattern → `SimDecay.from_pattern`; else lifetimes → `synthetic_decay`). Separately, the cramped **Channels** section (~14 flat q/background fields) is replaced by a compact custom `acq_channels` table — one row per colour (Green/Red/Yellow) with an enable checkbox and its `q ∥ / q ⊥ / bg ∥ / bg ⊥` columns bound to the model. Tests: `.../simulation/core/test/test_setup_widgets.py` (3: decay round-trip, load-pattern, channels binding) + the engine `test_decay.py` (3). See [subsystems/gui-autoform.md](/subsystems/gui-autoform.md).
* **Wired the canonical decay generator into the photon-stream simulators.** The acquisition TCSPC simulator (`plugins/core/acq/tcspc_devices/simulation/core/algorithms.py::build_engine`) previously ignored its `decay_lifetimes` param and never set `SimSpecies.decay`, so simulated photons had no lifetime structure — the synthetic decay generator was "missing in simulator/acq". It now builds each species' `SimDecay` from `decay_lifetimes[i]` (+ optional shared Gaussian IRF via `irf_fwhm_ns`) through the canonical `synthetic_decay` → `tttrlib.SimDecay.from_pattern`. The CLSM imaging simulator (`core/fluorescence/imaging/simulate.py::_lifetime_species`) was a second local duplicate (`np.convolve(np.exp(-t/τ), irf)`) — now also routed through `synthetic_decay`. Verified: longer lifetime shifts the simulated mean micro-time later (1 ns → bin ~31, 6 ns → ~149), IRF gives a prompt offset. Tests: new guarded `.../simulation/core/test/test_decay.py` (3, skip without tttrlib SimEngine); imaging-sim suite (6) still green. See [plugins/fcs.md](/plugins/fcs.md).
* **One canonical synthetic-decay generator + a full-stack `synthetic_decay` plugin; filter-sweep TODO.** Consolidated decay generation: `chisurf/core/fluorescence/decay.py` gained `synthetic_decay` / `synthetic_component_decay` (built on the shared `calculate_fluorescence_decay` + `tcspc/convolve.py` IRF kernels + `sample_decay_shot_noise`), replacing the FCS Filter Calculator's duplicate `api.py::synthetic_decay` (a local exponential + `np.convolve` reimplementation, now a thin re-export). New full-stack plugin `chisurf/plugins/fluorescence_decay/synthetic_decay/` (**Spectroscopy:Fluorescence Decay:Synthetic Decay Generator**): transport-agnostic `core/algorithms.py`, Click CLI (`synth-decay generate|component`), RPC services (`synthetic_decay.compute[_component]`), and an AutoForm GUI (editable lifetime-spectrum table + histogram/IRF/noise + live decay plot). The acquisition `core/experiments/tcspc/simulator.py` intentionally stays on the lower-level `calculate_fluorescence_decay` (rise terms / zero-lifetime components that the strict wrapper rejects). Tests: plugin `test_core.py` (7: core/CLI/RPC + a "uses core, not a duplicate" guard) + `test_widgets.py` (3); Filter-Calc suite still green. Also filed a **TODO (autoresearch)** in [plugins/fcs.md](/plugins/fcs.md): a fast auto-optimizing filter sweep maximizing species-filter contrast (→ anti-correlation contrast), with the `flc_2d` decay-unmixing machinery as a reuse candidate to drive/seed fFCS filter computation.
* **FCS Filter Calculator: unified Detectors + per-detector IRF table.** The detector-selection checkbox list and the confusing hidden per-detector IRF editor (a "Detector" combo + shared File/Width/Skew fields, where switching the combo changed nothing visible) are merged into one `DetectorIrfTableWidget` (`gui_parts/widgets.py`): a row per detector with a select checkbox, name, editable synthetic-IRF **Width** (FWHM ns) and **Skew**, and an **IRF** column whose `…` button loads a measured IRF (then becomes `✕` to unload). While an IRF is loaded, Width/Skew are grayed and auto-populated from the measured IRF (`irf_width_skew_ns` estimates FWHM + skewness). **Pol** on splits each detector into parallel/perpendicular rows with independent IRF/width/skew. Width/skew are now genuinely per-detector (previously global); `_nuisance_patterns` reads them (and the per-detector IRF path) from the table via `irf_path/width/skew(detector, role)`. Removed the `display_detector`/`irf_paths_by_detector`/`synthetic_irf_*`/`irf_path`/`set_detectors`/`detector_changed` surface from `CalculatorOptionsViewModel` and the Detector/File/Width/Skew rows from `calculator_options.view.json` (only the Pol/AP/IRF toggles remain); project save/load now persists `detector_irf` via `export_state`/`import_state`. 29 filter-calc tests pass; screenshot-verified (loaded-IRF row grays width/skew + shows ✕; Pol splits into ∥/⊥). See [plugins/fcs.md](/plugins/fcs.md).
* **Tooltip fix (show + fold) and removal of the redundant FCS "Nuisance" toggle.** (1) The app-wide tooltip filter previously rewrote a widget's tooltip on `QEvent.ToolTip` and passed the event through, which *suppressed* tooltip display. `_TooltipWrapFilter.eventFilter` now displays the folded tooltip itself via `QToolTip.showText(...)` and consumes the event (only when the widget has a tooltip, so parent→child inheritance still works) — tooltips show again and fold to `gui.tooltip.wrap_width`. (2) Removed the FCS Filter Calculator's `🚫 Nuisance` (`nuisance_rejection`) toggle: it was redundant with the AP/IRF toggles (which model afterpulse/scatter) and its only effect — excluding those rows from the correlation-facing output — is now **unconditional** (`reject_nuisance=True` hardwired at all compute sites; `api.py` keeps the param, default already True). The AP/IRF toggles stay; the Inputs row is now Pol / AP / IRF. Dropped the field from `CalculatorOptionsViewModel`, the toggle from `calculator_options.view.json`, and the project save/load persistence; tests updated. Verified: 29 filter-calc tests pass, Inputs shows 3 toggles, `to_channel_filters()` excludes nuisance (2 of 4 rows). See [plugins/fcs.md](/plugins/fcs.md).
* **App-wide auto-folding tooltips, yaml-configurable UI font size, and a settings deep-merge.** Long tooltips rendered as one screen-wide line. New `chisurf/gui/tooltip.py`: `wrap_tooltip()` folds tooltip text to a configurable width, and `install_tooltip_wrapping(app)` (called from `get_app`) installs an application event filter that folds *every* widget tooltip on first hover — so any `setToolTip` in ChiSurf is folded without touching the call site. AutoForm now folds section descriptions through the same helper (previously the form's label column kept the raw unwrapped text). Config: `gui.tooltip.{enabled,wrap_width}` (default 72) in `settings_chisurf.yaml`. Separately, the hardcoded macOS global font point size is now `gui.application_font_size` (default 13; 0 = platform default). **Root-cause fix enabling all this:** `get_chisurf_settings` now deep-merges the packaged default YAML *underneath* the user's settings file, so keys added in newer releases resolve with their defaults on existing installs (the loader previously used the user file verbatim, so new keys were invisible) while any user-set value still wins. Tests: `test/gui/test_tooltip_wrap.py` (5, incl. the deep-merge). See [workflows/build-and-env.md](/workflows/build-and-env.md), [subsystems/gui-autoform.md](/subsystems/gui-autoform.md).
* **Shared compact `SetupSelector` widget + FCS Filter Calculator UI polish.** New reusable `chisurf/gui/widgets/setup_selector.py::SetupSelector` — a compact detector-setup chooser (combo + `↻` reload + optional muted detector summary) that emits `setupChanged(str)` and is backed by `load_detector_setups` (injectable loader for tests/RPC). It replaces the copy-pasted `QLabel("Setup:") + QComboBox + reload` pattern the survey found in ~8 sites. Adopted in the FCS Filter Calculator (drops the "Definitions: Detector Def" / "Setup:" labels for a single tight row) and in `burst_fcs_correlator` (removed its hand-rolled combo + `load_detector_setups` plumbing). Remaining hand-rolled sites to migrate: the acquisition-control experiment widgets (`gui/widgets/experiments/{tcspc,pch,rics,pda}` — richer setup+detector+routine controls), `fcs_channel_preset` (the setup *editor*), `burst_bva` (mirror combo), `burst_fcs_correlator/wizard.py` (legacy). Filter Calculator also: the cryptic `⌫ Reject` toggle is now `🚫 Nuisance` with a clearer tooltip (keep AP/scatter filters to absorb nuisance photons but drop those rows from the correlation-facing output); and the Reconstruction/decay plot now overlays each detector's IRF/scatter pattern (cyan dotted, rescaled to the decay peak, near-zero tail masked so the log axis stays sane). Tests: `test/gui/test_setup_selector.py` (3) + the Filter Calculator suite (29) pass. See [subsystems/gui-autoform.md](/subsystems/gui-autoform.md), [plugins/fcs.md](/plugins/fcs.md).

* **pixi now always uses the freshly-built local tttrlib (fixes missing `SimEngine`).** The Lifetime-FCS Sim crashed with `module 'tttrlib' has no attribute 'SimEngine'` because `pixi run chisurf` used the conda `tttrlib` (bioconda 0.26.2 — its files had also been clobbered by an old 0.0.0 manual install), and `SimEngine` (the PRD-005 photon simulator) is in the *unreleased* 0.27.0 source, 78 commits past the v0.26.2 tag. New `build_tools/build_tttrlib.py` + `build-tttrlib` pixi task build the local tttrlib source *over* the conda package; it is wired into `build-extensions` (and `build-extensions` is now a `depends-on` of the `chisurf` launch task), so pixi always uses the most recent build. It no-ops when the developer-local, gitignored `modules/tttrlib` symlink (→ the tttrlib checkout, added like `modules/imp-tricks`) is absent, so CI/other machines keep the conda package. macOS specifics: links the env `libomp` into the SWIG module (else it loads with a flat-namespace `___kmpc_barrier` error) and builds in an isolated gitignored `build/tttrlib` tree (reusing tttrlib's in-source build dir across flag changes regenerates a stale SWIG wrapper that fails to compile). Verified: clean+idempotent builds install tttrlib 0.27.0 with `SimEngine`, and `simulate_lifetime_fcs` runs in the pixi test env. See [subsystems/compiled-modules.md](/subsystems/compiled-modules.md), [workflows/build-and-env.md](/workflows/build-and-env.md).

Channel Definitions → 2. Files & Steps → 3. Photon/Burst Filter → 4. Correlator → 5. FCS Merger` and opens on the file-drop step. Panel row indices are unchanged (channel-def replaces detector at row 0), so the existing carry-over test still holds. (2) **Lifetime-filter (FLCS) wiring in `4. Correlator`** — `set_lifetime_filters` was previously dead code; added a `lifetime_filter_controls` AutoForm section (`🧬 Load filters… / ✖ Unload`) that loads an fFCS `FilterResult` JSON (`to_channel_filters()`, nuisance excluded) or a `.npy`/`.npz` matrix via `CorrelatorSettingsModel.load_lifetime_filter_file`. In *species mode* the `channel_combos` A/B selectors list filter species (labels from metadata or `Species N`) and set `_species_a`/`_species_b`; `_correlate_lifetime_filtered` now correlates only the selected pair (ACF when A=B, CCF when A≠B) by subsetting the filter rows (`_subset_species`, handles 2-D/3-D/`{channel: 2-D}`). A confocal sm measurement is mostly empty focus, so the photons a sliding-window burst search *rejects* are the built-in scatter/background: `extract_irf_background` inverts the burst search and, per detector, (a) fits the non-burst interphoton-time tail for the background rate (kHz, reusing `background.estimate_background_from_interphoton_times`) and (b) histograms the non-burst micro-times over the full laser period, subtracts a robust flat dark-count floor (low quantile) and normalises the remainder to a scatter-derived IRF. * **Pixel-wise FLIM MLE: C++ batch fit + threaded dispatch makes fitting scale (in-process, ~4×).** Superseded the earlier fork-multiprocessing approach after finding the real bottleneck. Per-fit threading did not scale (flat 1.0× on 2–8 threads) even with the GIL released around `DecayFit23::fit`: each fit releases the GIL for <1 ms, and the **per-fit GIL-handoff convoy** serialises the threads. Ruled out the macOS nano allocator (`MallocNanoZone=0` unchanged) and `thread_local`/TLS (plain `static` unchanged); a BLAS `np.dot` control thread-scales 4× in the same process, so it was the fit, not the environment. Fix: a new tttrlib batch entry point **`DecayFit23::fit_matrix`** (committed in tttrlib `1650cf67`) fits a whole `(n_rows × 2·n_ch)` matrix in one C++ call with the GIL released for the *entire* loop; rebuild the arm64 editable install per [[tttrlib-editable-rebuild]] (note the SWIG-regen gotcha recorded there — `touch ext/python/tttrlib.i` after editing an included `.i`). ChiSurf side: `Fit2x.fit_many` wraps it, and `chisurf/core/fluorescence/mle/parallel.py::fit_matrix_threaded` splits rows across a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (each thread its own `Fit2x`) — **no multiprocessing**, so no fork/spawn fragility and safe inside the Qt GUI. `img_pixel_mle/core/pixel_mle.py` now dispatches through it (`n_workers` control, `_MIN_ROWS_FOR_THREADS` gate). Measured: batch threading 2t 1.95× / 4t 3.74× / 8t 4.63×, bit-identical to single-fit; end-to-end A/B on `beads.ptu` baseline→+fast 1.15×→+threaded(7w) **4.08×**, results identical. Tests updated (`test_threaded_matches_serial`); benchmark `test/benchmarks/benchmark_pixel_mle.py`. Replaces the fork-MP `fit_matrix_parallel`. See [plugins/imaging.md](/plugins/imaging.md) and the `fit2x` harness in [subsystems/fitting.md](/subsystems/fitting.md).
* **fit2x fit itself ~5× faster (Brent 1-D + objective hoist), bit-close.** Two tttrlib changes to the fit23 estimator (commits `1650cf67`/`f133e231`/`96924906` there). (1) **Objective hoist** — `targetf` recomputed the data-only signal integrals (`Sp/Ss/B`) on every objective evaluation, but they are constant during a fit (only the soft-BIFL `Bexpected` depends on parameters); recompute only when soft-BIFL is active → ~10% faster, **max\|Δτ\|=0** over 120 real decays vs the unmodified build. (2) **Brent 1-D minimiser** — when only τ is free (γ/r0/ρ fixed: the pixel-wise FLIM / burst-lifetime case) the fit is 1-D, so a bounded derivative-free Brent minimiser replaces the general BFGS-with-numerical-gradients engine (~5× fewer objective evaluations). Verified on real FLIM decays: same MLE minimum to 6 sig-figs (max\|Δτ\|=5e-5, rel 6e-6 — far below lifetime measurement precision), **0.88 → 0.18 ms/fit (~4.9×)**; BFGS unchanged for all other free-parameter combinations. (3) **NEON 2-channel convolution** (commit `eee0eebf`) — the fit23 model convolves parallel/perpendicular channels that share lifetimes; the per-channel recurrence is latency-bound and un-vectorisable *within* a channel, but the two channels run together in `float64x2` lanes (`fconv_per_cs_2ch`, scalar two-call fallback off-ARM) → another **~1.5×** (0.18 → 0.12 ms), numerically identical (median τ matches the scalar path to full precision). So the fit itself is **~7.3×** (0.88 → 0.12 ms) and, with the batch/threaded dispatch, **≈33× throughput** on the pixel-MLE fit vs the original per-fit BFGS+scalar-convolution path. Tried but dropped: `-ffast-math -mcpu=native` gave only ~6% (the recurrence dominates and can't reassociate) — not worth global FP-semantics changes. float32 would help little here (working set is L1-resident and the 2 channels already fill the NEON register), so not pursued.

Missing entries invoke the shared TCSPC synthetic-IRF path: prompt position and FWHM are searched against that detector's mixed decay while molecular, constant-afterpulse, and IRF-scatter amplitudes are constrained non-negative; parallel/perpendicular decays receive separate fitted patterns. The preloaded fast/slow patterns are now convolved with detector-distinct synthetic IRFs, and each 100,000-photon detector mixture includes both IRF scatter and constant afterpulse counts. Per-detector IRF paths, synthetic starting parameters, and inline example decays persist in projects. Verification: 33 focused tests pass, including synthetic-IRF recovery and distinct detector patterns/mixtures.

Filter calculation and non-negative unmixing now include enabled nuisance components, report their fitted counts independently, draw stable diagnostic filter colors, and preserve them in projects/results. * **Central intensity/decay computation is now an explicit design objective; FCS Filter Calculator begins the convergence.** Documented the north-star in [Fluorescence Domain](/subsystems/fluorescence-domain.md): detector-resolved intensities, TCSPC decays, and reusable patterns should have one Qt-free computation path owning IRF, polarization, pile-up, background/scatter, detector response, excitation/emission mixing, and crosstalk; fits, simulators, FCS/FLCS, imaging, and exporters consume it instead of duplicating forward models. Added `chisurf/core/fluorescence/decay.py` as an incremental adapter over the established fit/model stack (`lifetime_spectrum_from_model`, `compute_model_decay`, `compute_detector_patterns_from_fit`). Plugin-local ideal/distribution generation remains a headless fallback, reusing ChiSurf's existing FRET distance/rate functions. Focused verification: 18 tests pass; critical Ruff checks, compileall, diff checks, and table-dialog visual verdict pass.
* **Calibration: general excitation/emission crosstalk-matrix correction (Hellenkamp is the 2-colour special case) (continuation 3).** Per the steer that the scalar α/β/γ/δ are only a special case and the general excitation/emission crosstalk matrices must still work, added the general matrix correction. New `es.py::corrected_es_general(intensity, excitation, emission)` corrects straight from the two light-path matrices — **excitation** `X[l,k]` (laser→chromophore) and **emission** `D[k,m]` (chromophore→detector) — in three steps: (1) un-mix emission `e[l,:] = I[l,:] @ D⁻¹` (removes *all* spectral crosstalk incl. acceptor↔acceptor bleed, and folds the detection/QY ratio into the `D` diagonal so **no explicit γ** appears), (2) subtract direct excitation `F[l,k] = e[l,k] − (X[l,k]/X[k,k])·e[k,k]`, (3) coupled donor budget `E[l,k] = F[l,k]/(e[l,l] + Σ_a F[l,a])`. It reduces **algebraically** to `corrected_es` for two colours (`D=[[1,α],[0,γ]]`, `X=[[1,δ],[0,1]]`) and recovers exact E for ≥3 chromophores with inter-acceptor leakage the scalar path cannot express. `calibration.py::crosstalk_matrices_from_lightpath` builds `X`,`D` from a `get_crosstalk_matrices()` payload (folding QY/detection efficiency into `D`), and `general_correction_from_lightpath` wraps the whole path. This resolves the previously-deferred "multi-acceptor cross-leakage" item; `corrected_es_matrix` stays as the scalar fast path when there is no inter-acceptor bleed. Tests: `test/fitting/test_general_correction.py` (8: 2-colour reduction == `corrected_es`, 3-colour with acceptor↔acceptor bleed exact, scalar-path-is-biased contrast, light-path-payload path) — 43 calibration/crosstalk tests pass, ruff clean (arm64). Docs: `docs/FRET calibration.md` gains a "The general case: crosstalk matrices" section (scalar factors reframed as the two-colour reduction); OKF [references/fret-calibration.md](/references/fret-calibration.md) updated (general-form bullet; cross-leakage moved from "missing" to done). **Stable un-mixing follow-up:** the emission un-mix (step 1, `I[l,:] @ D⁻¹`) is the numerically delicate part — for strong spectral overlap `D` is ill-conditioned, so the plain pseudo-inverse amplifies shot noise and returns unphysical **negative** emissions. Added a selectable `unmix` argument to `corrected_es_general`/`general_correction_from_lightpath`: `"naive"` (fast vectorized pinv, default) vs `"stable"` (**non-negative least squares** per burst — enforces `e≥0`, robust to overlap), plus an optional `ridge` (Tikhonov) damping usable with either. Both share `crosstalk.invert_mixing`, which was extended with a `ridge` Tikhonov parameter (closed form for the linear solve, augmented-system for NNLS) — also available to the phasor-FLIM unmix. Method choice follows the standard fluorescence-microscopy unmixing literature (NNLS/fully-constrained LU for positivity; Tikhonov to fix ill-conditioning). Tests grew to 13 (naive==stable on clean data; NNLS non-negative where pinv goes negative on ill-conditioned noisy data; ridge lowers burst-to-burst E variance; invalid-method guard) — 48 calibration/crosstalk tests pass, ruff clean (arm64). Docs gain a "Naive vs. stable un-mixing" subsection. **Photon-statistics + ndx follow-up:** (checked the user-supplied `nishio-laboratory/lambda_split` repo — it is an unrelated LLM/diffusion inference-splitting project, not the fluorescence "λSplit" spectral-unmixing paper; removed from junk.) (1) **Integer, statistics-preserving un-mixing** `crosstalk.photon_shuffle_unmix(counts, matrix, *, abundances, seed)` — reassigns each detected photon to a source by a multinomial draw (`P(k|m) ∝ a_k·B[k,m]`, `B`=row-normalised emission spectral shape, `a_k`=NNLS abundance prior), giving a non-negative **integer** per-source photon stream that preserves the total count exactly and the Poisson shot-noise (multinomial thinning of Poisson is Poisson) — for BVA/MLE/burst-variance downstream; expectation == the continuous Richardson–Lucy/EM unmix (unbiased). Vectorised over bursts by a binomial chain. `test_photon_shuffle.py` (5). (2) **ndx stable/shuffle injection** — ndx corrects FRET with scalar string-equations and exposes **no compute hook** (confirmed by exploring the in-tree `modules/ndxplorer` submodule), so `push_unmixed_columns_to_ndx(ndx, *, emission, channel_columns, source_labels, unmix="stable"|"shuffle", seed, rate_columns)` reads the measured per-channel count columns, un-mixes them (NNLS default / integer shuffle) with the light-path emission matrix, and injects leakage-free per-source photon+rate columns back as **new** columns (native ndx columns/equations untouched → no double-correction). Per user steer, **no hard-coded detector names** — caller supplies the emission matrix + column names + source labels (from `crosstalk_matrices_from_lightpath`), general to any N-colour setup. `test_calibration_ndx_bridge.py` grew +3. Total 56 calibration/crosstalk tests pass, ruff clean (arm64). Docs gain "Preserving photon-counting statistics" + "ndxplorer: stable / shuffle un-mixing" sections; OKF [references/fret-calibration.md](/references/fret-calibration.md) updated. **Headless real-engine ndx test (per steer "make it possible to drive tests headless"):** the stub-only ndx coverage is now complemented by `test/fio/test_ndxplorer_unmix_headless.py`, which drives ndx's **actual** `DataSource` + real `mfd.equations.yaml`/`mfd.constants.json` with **no Qt window / no display** — it self-adds the in-tree `modules/ndxplorer` submodule to `sys.path`, sets `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`, `importorskip`s when absent (mirrors the existing `test/fio/test_ndxplorer_rpc_bridge.py` pattern), and asserts (a) a pushed `gamma` genuinely changes the engine-computed `FRET efficiency` column, (b) injected unmixed columns are computable by ndx's own equation engine, (c) shuffle columns are integer + count-preserving through the real `DataSource`. 3 headless tests pass (arm64, offscreen).
* **Pixel-wise FLIM MLE throughput: vectorised extraction + multiprocessing fits + GIL release (A/B benchmarked).** Two optimisations to `img_pixel_mle/core/pixel_mle.py`, both A/B-verified to give **identical** per-pixel lifetimes. (1) **Vectorised extraction** — replaced the per-pixel Python `tttr_indices`+`np.bincount` loop with one `CLSMImage.get_fluorescence_decay` C++ call building the whole per-pixel histogram stack (matches bincount exactly; the returned uint8 is guarded — saturation auto-falls-back to the exact bincount engine). An `engine` switch (`"auto"`/`"fast"`/`"loop"`) selects it. (2) **Multiprocessing fits** — the per-pixel `Fit23` calls (the dominant cost) now run across worker processes over a shared-memory copy of the histogram matrix, via a new reusable, Qt-free helper `chisurf/core/fluorescence/mle/parallel.py::fit_matrix_parallel` (built on the `fit2x` harness). It uses the **fork** start method so workers inherit the parent's imports — avoiding a hang where `spawn` re-imports the deep plugin/GUI package chain in a subprocess — with a serial fallback on any failure and an `n_workers` control. **Investigation & tttrlib change:** per the "let it release GIL" steer, added GIL release around `DecayFit{23,24,25,26}::fit` in tttrlib (`ext/python/DecayFit*.i`, committed there `bebd7bb9`; rebuild the arm64 editable install per [[tttrlib-editable-rebuild]]). Threaded fits are now **bit-identical** to serial (the fit's per-call state is `static thread_local`), but in-process threading still does **not scale** on macOS (the fit serialises on an internal per-thread-state access path; a BLAS `np.dot` control thread-scales 4× in the same env, so it is the fit, not the environment) — hence multiprocessing for throughput. The GIL release is kept as the correct, safe precondition (helps latency/GUI-responsiveness; enables future threading if the C++ serialiser is removed). **A/B benchmark** `test/benchmarks/benchmark_pixel_mle.py` on real FLIM `tttr-data/imaging/pq/Microtime200_HH400/beads.ptu`: baseline (loop, serial) → +fast extraction 1.13× → +parallel (7 workers) **2.58×**, results identical. Tests: `img_pixel_mle/test/test_pixel_mle_core.py` gains fast-vs-loop and MP-vs-serial equivalence (6 pass); benchmark has a `slow` equivalence+speedup test. See [plugins/imaging.md](/plugins/imaging.md) and the `fit2x` harness in [subsystems/fitting.md](/subsystems/fitting.md).
* **ALEX analysis of Shimon Weiss lab `.sm` files: auto window-split + end-to-end test/example (chisurf and tttrlib).** Shimon Weiss lab single-molecule `.sm` files (tttrlib `SM` container, record type 11) store only a macro-time and a routing channel — no TCSPC micro-time. Micro-second ALEX encodes the green/red laser alternation in the macro-time clock, so `TTTR.alex_to_microtime(period, shift)` folds it into a synthetic micro-time (`micro = (macro − shift) % period`) that recovers the excitation window by gating, exactly like PIE. Added **automatic green/red window detection** to the ALEX plugin core (`chisurf/plugins/tttr/ptu_alex_creator/core`): `auto_alex_windows(...)` histograms the folded phase, finds the two laser-on plateaus as the two largest occupied runs (circular `_contiguous_runs`), **guard-bands each edge** (default 6%) to drop the laser rise/fall photons (some photon loss is intended — ~88% retention), and labels the donor-brighter window "green"; `alex_stream_masks(...)` returns the DD/DA/AA/AD boolean masks. It raises `ValueError` on continuous-wave data (single fully-occupied period). Verified the full smFRET path works with `.sm` input: load → `apply_alex` → auto-split → all-photon burst search → per-burst DD/DA/AA counting → apparent/corrected E and S via [`burst/es.py`](/subsystems/fluorescence-domain.md) (`apparent_es`/`corrected_es`). Because the shipped reference `tttr-data/sm/data.sm` is a continuous-wave, donor-dominated file (60 s, ch0≫ch1, no alternation — confirmed by FFT/fold-contrast analysis showing no laser-alternation frequency), tests use a **synthetic ground-truth ALEX stream with realistic laser windows (interior plateaus + rise/fall gaps + edge smear) round-tripped through the `.sm` container** (set `MeasDesc_GlobalResolution` tag so the written file reads back at 12.5 ns) to check window recovery + E/S recovery, and additionally load the real file to prove reading + burst search. Auto-split recovers windows inside the true laser bounds and two injected populations (600 bursts, E≈0.20/0.80, S≈0.55). New: `test/fitting/test_alex_sm.py` (7), `examples/alex_sm_es.py`; and in tttrlib `test/python/burstfilter/test_alex_sm.py` (7, with a standalone copy of the auto-split helper) + `examples/single_molecule/plot_alex_sm.py` (sphinx-gallery, phase histogram with detected windows + E-S 2D histogram). Only new core code is the `auto_alex_windows`/`alex_stream_masks` helpers; the ALEX/.sm folding + es capability already existed.
* **Molecule-wise MLE (`sm_image_mle`): reworked onto a Qt-free core + AutoForm GUI, verified against tttrlib-simulated CLSM images.** The plugin's real algorithm (segment single molecules from a CLSM intensity image, build a per-molecule VV/VH histogram, fit each by Fit23 Poisson MLE) lived in a ~790-line monolithic `click` script `sm_image_mle.py`, and the "API layer" (`api/molecule_mle.py`) shelled out to that script **as a subprocess per PTU file** — so every consumer re-parsed CLI args, and the GUI was an old-style `QMainWindow` (drag-drop `FileListWidget` + `Worker(QThread)` running the subprocess + a `BrowserWidget` reading PNGs off disk). Extracted the computation into a new Qt-free `chisurf/plugins/microscopy/sm_image_mle/core/molecule_mle.py` — `MoleculeMleSettings`, `MoleculeMleResult`, `segment_molecules` (watershed), `build_irf_vv_vh`/`compute_g_factor`, `fit_molecules(tttr, settings, clsm=…)` / `fit_molecules_from_files` — built on the shared [`fit2x` harness](/subsystems/fitting.md) (`Fit2x`/`assemble_vv_vh`), returning a per-molecule DataFrame + label/intensity images + centroids (no more matplotlib PNG dumps or TSV writes in the compute layer). `api/molecule_mle.py::analyze_request` now runs the core **in-process** (loop files → per-file `molecule_data.tsv` + merged `joint_output.tsv`), mirroring the pixel-wise sibling. Replaced the whole old GUI with an **AutoForm view.json** (`gui/molecule_mle.view.json`) over a Qt-free `MoleculeMleViewModel` (`path_list` file/IRF inputs, value/toggle settings, a `▶ Run` `button_row` launched on a `QThreadPool` worker, an `image` dock showing the segmentation with green molecule-centroid markers, and a `table` of per-molecule fits); `gui/tool.py::SmImageMleTool` is now a thin `AutoForm`-hosting `QWidget`. Deleted the monolith `sm_image_mle.py` and the dead `cli.py` shim (the `cli/` package shadowed it); fixed `cli/__init__.py` to actually export `cli`. **Verified against tttrlib-simulated CLSM images** (`SimEngine`/`SimScanner` raster of two immobile fluorophores with τ=1.0/3.5 ns → segment → fit recovers τ≈1.0/3.55 ns), and the GUI headless-screenshot-verified (image + markers + table render the simulated result). Tests (arm64): new `test/test_molecule_mle_core.py` (simulate→segment→fit, 3), `test/test_api_orchestration.py` (per-file + joint TSV, warnings, 2), rewritten `test/test_widgets.py` (view-model bindings, view-spec load, AutoForm tool, 3) — 8 pass. Manifest bumped to 2.1.0. See [plugins/imaging.md](/plugins/imaging.md) and the `fit2x` harness in [subsystems/fitting.md](/subsystems/fitting.md).
* **Calibration: reference-sample α/δ + multi-chromophore N-cube + confirmed GUI parameter-link (continuation 2).** Completed the calibration methodology and generalised it beyond two colours. (1) **Reference-sample estimators** (`chisurf/core/fluorescence/fret/calibration.py`): `leakage_from_donor_only` (α from a donor-only sample), `direct_excitation_from_acceptor_only` (δ from an acceptor-only sample), and `calibrate_from_samples` orchestrating the full Hellenkamp procedure (α from donor-only, δ from acceptor-only, γ/β from the FRET E-S fit, optional prior-regularized refine) — α/δ are now data-driven, not only the light-path prior (`test_calibration_samples.py`, recovers known α=0.08/δ=0.05/γ=1.4). (2) **Multi-chromophore (N-cube) correction** `es.py::corrected_es_matrix(intensity, gamma, alpha, delta, …)` — generalises the three-cube to an N×N `I_ij` matrix using the **coupled donor budget** `E_ij = (F_ij/γ_ij)/(F_ii + Σ_k F_ik/γ_ik)`, recovering each pairwise efficiency exactly when one donor is quenched by several acceptors (the naive pairwise formula biases `E_ij → E_ij/(1−E_ik)`); reduces exactly to `corrected_es` for two chromophores (`test_multi_chromophore.py`: N=2 reduction + 3-color exact recovery + documents the bias). (3) **GUI parameter-link auto-wired** — confirmed `ChiSurfAPI.list_fits()` serializes the registered `CalibrationFit` with its factors (the same source the parameter-link menu reads), so the shared calibration appears as a link target with no extra Qt (`test_calibration_shared.py`). 37 calibration/crosstalk tests pass, ruff clean (arm64). Only remaining: a one-click ndx toolbar push button and per-pixel/FLIM reuse (headless cores + ndx bridge already cover the substance) — see [references/fret-calibration.md](/references/fret-calibration.md). Added a **user-facing docs page** `docs/FRET calibration.md` (Sphinx toctree in `docs/index.rst`) — theory (Hellenkamp α/β/γ/δ, I_ij channels, E/S formulas), the two factor-sourcing routes (light-path prior→posterior; donor-only/acceptor-only reference samples), the multi-chromophore coupled-budget correction, global-analysis linking + ndx push, and simulation-based validation, with code examples and references (Hellenkamp 2018, Lee 2005).
* **Calibration: session-shared cross-fit linking + ndx bridge + Hellenkamp nomenclature (continuation).** Built the two cross-cutting pieces of the calibration vision on top of the calibration core (see the calibration entry below). (1) **Session-shared calibration for global analysis** — `CalibrationFit` wraps `CalibrationParameters` as a dataset-free pseudo-fit (minimal `model`+`unique_identifier` contract); `register_calibration`/`unregister_calibration` add it to `cs.fits` (+ project registry) so it appears in the parameter-link UI, and `link_to_calibration(param, calib, factor)` links any fit's correction parameter to the shared factor via chinet-port identity — refining one calibration updates every linked fit. (2) **ndxplorer bridge** — `calibration_to_ndx_constants` maps the posterior factors onto ndx's MFD constants (inverting ndx's effective `gamma=(PhiA/PhiD)/(gG/gR)`; ndx's `beta`≡direct-excitation δ), and `chisurf/plugins/ndxplorer/calibration_bridge.py::push_calibration_to_ndx` writes them into an in-process ndx window's `constants` and recomputes, so ndx's derived FRET uses the data-optimized calibration. (3) **Hellenkamp 2018 nomenclature + multi-chromophore convention** — renamed the calibration factors to α/β/γ/δ uniformly (**added the previously-missing β** excitation-flux ratio to `CalibrationParameters` and the `es.py` stoichiometry `S=(γF+F_da)/(γF+F_da+F_aa/β)`; `refine_calibration` also recovers β from the E-S fit). Channels use the general numeric convention `I_ij` = emission of chromophore j under excitation of i (donor 1, acceptor 2, second acceptor 3, …) to generalise to multi-chromophore systems, with friendly `i_dd`/`i_da`/`i_aa` (≡`I_11`/`I_12`/`I_22`) aliases kept in the user-facing API. Tests: `test/fitting/test_calibration_shared.py` (3), `test_calibration_ndx_bridge.py` (3), plus the updated `test_fret_calibration.py`/`test_calibration_simulation.py` — 27 calibration+crosstalk tests pass, ruff clean (arm64). OKF: [references/fret-calibration.md](/references/fret-calibration.md) updated (shared-fit + ndx bridge moved from "missing" to done; naming section added).

Docs: [subsystems/fitting.md](/subsystems/fitting.md), [PRD-61](/prds/prd-61.md).
* **Generalized fitting with parameter priors — bounds as priors (PRD-61).** Generalized the fit objective from least squares to maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) and Bayesian sampling by letting any parameter carry a **prior**, with hard **bounds implemented as the degenerate `UniformPrior`**. New Qt-free module `chisurf/core/fitting/priors.py`: a `Prior` ABC (`lnpdf`, `residuals` for the LM/MAP contribution, `support` for hard optimiser bounds, `mode`, `get_state`, `combine`/`__mul__`) with families `UniformPrior`, `NormalPrior`, `TruncatedNormalPrior`, `HalfNormalPrior`, `LogNormalPrior`, `ExponentialPrior`, `GammaPrior`, `BetaPrior`, and `CallablePrior` — the most general form wrapping any `logpdf(x)` callback (runtime-only, not serialised); `as_prior` coerces a Prior/callable/state-dict and `prior_from_state`+`PRIOR_REGISTRY` deserialise. **MAP**: `_prior_residuals` appends each free parameter's `prior.residuals(value)` to the residual vector when `get_wres(..., include_priors=True)` (Gaussian → Tikhonov `(θ−μ)/σ`; general → signed deviance `sign(θ−mode)·√(−2·Δlnpdf)`, the same reduction as the Poisson `2I*` residuals), so the existing `leastsqbound` LM engine minimises `χ²−2·ln p(θ)` unchanged; `Fit.run`/`FitGroup.run` enable it, `get_chi2` stays data-only. **MCMC**: `lnprior` now sums per-parameter `prior.lnpdf` (uniform-box fallback). **Conjugacy**: `Prior.combine` returns closed-form conjugates (`Normal×Normal` precision-weighted, `Gamma×Gamma`, `Beta×Beta`, `Normal×Uniform → TruncatedNormal`) and a generic `ProductPrior` (summed log-densities, concatenated residuals) otherwise. **chinet**: the distribution prior's spec is stored on the parameter's `chinet.Port` (`port.prior`, in the port document/JSON) so it round-trips through pickle/JSON (`modules/chinet/chinet/port.py`); `Parameter.prior` unifies bounds and priors (live callable object in memory, serialisable spec mirrored to the port, bound surfaced as `UniformPrior`). **RPC**: new `parameter.set_prior` threaded `fitting_client` → `protocol` → `server_methods.json` → `services.parameters.set_parameter_prior` → `Parameter.prior`, plus `Fit.set_parameter_prior`. **GUI**: the per-parameter popup (`chisurf/gui/widgets/fitting/parameter_widgets.py`) replaces the raw bound-box inputs with a prior-type radio selector (**Box** default with inline lower/upper bounds, **Gaussian**, **Log-normal**, **Custom…**) and a modal `PriorEditorDialog` for advanced per-distribution parameters (all families incl. Gamma/Beta/etc). Tests (arm64): `test/fitting/test_priors.py` (41 — families, callback, conjugate combination, MAP bias/recovery, port/pickle round-trip), `test/gui/test_parameter_prior_widget.py` (7, headless, screenshot-verified), client + protocol/service contract + chinet suites green. Also fixed a latent `Parameter.get_state` bug where an unbounded port's `(None, None)` bounds raised in `float()`. Follow-ups: AutoForm/view-spec prior surface; optional named-callback registry for persistence. See [subsystems/fitting.md](/subsystems/fitting.md), [subsystems/parameters.md](/subsystems/parameters.md), and [PRD-61](/prds/prd-61.md).

## 2026-07-16
* **smFRET calibration core: light-path prior → data-optimized posterior (accurate FRET).** Calibration factors (detection/QY ratio `gamma`, donor leakage `alpha`, direct acceptor excitation `delta`, backgrounds, `R0`) are now proper `FittingParameter`s whose **prior** comes from the light-path calculator and whose **posterior** comes from optimizing against burst data — plugging into the (already-wired) priors machinery (`chisurf/core/fitting/priors.py`, `Fit.set_parameter_prior`, `_prior_residuals`/`lnprob`). New Qt-free `chisurf/core/fluorescence/fret/calibration.py`: `CalibrationParameters(FittingParameterGroup)`; `lightpath_correction_factors`/`set_priors_from_lightpath` (compute `gamma=(gR·cRA·QYA)/(gG·cGD·QYD)`, `alpha`, `delta` from a `get_crosstalk_matrices()` payload via `crosstalk.matrix_from_payload` + the `pda/nusiance.py` algebra, and attach `NormalPrior`/`TruncatedNormalPrior`); `global_es_correction` (data `gamma` from the E-S population linear fit `1/S=Ω+Σ·E`, Lee 2005 / Hellenkamp 2018) and `refine_calibration` (the **posterior**: precision-weighted Bayesian combination of the bootstrapped data estimate and the light-path prior — strong data→data, weak data→prior). New `chisurf/core/fluorescence/burst/es.py`: `apparent_es` + `corrected_es` (three-cube E and, newly, ALEX/PIE stoichiometry `S`, reusing `crosstalk.correct_three_cube`). `BurstWorkflow.simulate(gamma=…)` now bakes a known detection factor into the tttrlib photon simulation (red-brightness scaled by gamma), recorded on `GroundTruth.gamma`, so recovery is validated end-to-end. Fixed a latent bug surfaced en route (already covered) — the `nusiance` decorator's Py2 `func_globals`. Tests: `test/fitting/test_fret_calibration.py` (8: factors, priors, E/S recovery, gamma recovery, strong-vs-weak-data posterior) + `test/plugins/burst/test_calibration_simulation.py` (2, end-to-end: simulate known gamma → burst-select → BVA proximity ratio → corrected E recovers the true 0.25/0.75) — all pass (arm64). Example notebook `chisurf/plugins/burst/burst_analysis/examples/FRET_Calibration.ipynb` (runs end-to-end: light-path prior → simulate → E-S plot apparent-vs-corrected → layered calibration → tttrlib-sim recovery). ## 2026-07-13
* **General non-programmer facade for the MMFDB burst workflow.** Added `chisurf/plugins/burst/burst_analysis/api/workflow.py` — a Qt-free `BurstWorkflow` facade that collapses the whole remote pipeline (start/connect MMFDB server + login → register dataset(s) → fetch-by-handle → burst selection → BVA → H2MM) into one plain-English line per step, so a bench scientist needs no settings dataclasses, object UUIDs, or TTTR bookkeeping. `BurstWorkflow.demo()` spins up a private in-process server for tutorials; `.connect(url, user, password)` targets a real deployment. Generality: a declarable `Setup` of named `Detector`s (routing channels + optional micro-time windows), built via `Setup.from_channels(green=…, red=…, yellow=…)` for any number of dyes and mirroring ChiSurf's `{name:{chs,micro_time_ranges}}` model. FRET is not baked into the setup (no donor/acceptor or "two-colour" naming) — the pair is chosen per analysis (`bva("green","red")`, `h2mm(donor=…, acceptor=…)`), defaulting to the first two detectors, while H2MM models every detector as a stream (true N-colour). Optional/inferred `file_type`; `register_all` + multi-dataset `select_bursts`; and a selectable search `method` (default `"burst"` sliding-window, which — unlike the old `filter_active=False` grouping — actually honours `min_photons`). `Bursts.bva()` / `.h2mm(states=…)` return `Bva`/`H2mm` results carrying `.plot()`, `.summary()`, `mean_proximity_ratio`, `dynamic_fraction`. Rewrote `modules/mmfdb/examples/mmfdb_00_overview.ipynb` (executes end-to-end: 3 datasets, 488 bursts, BVA 41 % dynamic fraction, H2MM 3-state fit) and `test/plugins/burst/test_mmfdb_burst_workflow.py` (8 tests against a live demo server: handle round-trip, multi-dataset selection, explicit-vs-default setup, three-colour setup with a chosen FRET pair, micro-time-gated detectors, setup validation, BVA ranges, deterministic 2-state H2MM).

* **Burst — H2MM model-selection early-stopping + SIMD/scan-trick dead-ends recorded.** Explored further *algorithmic* speed-ups now that per-fit exact EM is at the roofline. (1) **Early-stop the state-count scan** (`scan_states`/`analyze` opt-in `patience`): the BIC/ICL curve is U-shaped and the over-fit high-`k` fits are the *most expensive* — a redundant state makes a flat likelihood ridge so they run to `max_iter` without converging (measured: k=1..5 on 2-state data took 5/24/500/500/500 maps). Stopping once the criterion has risen for `patience+1` counts gave a **measured 1.65× faster scan** with identical selection; `patience=None` (default) is unchanged. (2) **SIMD confirmed a dead end by experiment:** reordering the forward matmul from a `k`-reduction to a supposedly-SIMD-friendly `i`-inner AXPY made it **0.3–0.7× (slower)** at n=2..5 — LLVM already register-optimises the small unrolled reduction, and over-burst SoA batching is structurally blocked by H2MM's variable-Δt design (each burst/photon needs a *different* transition matrix → per-lane gather, no uniform SIMD op). Not adopted. (3) Skipping per-`k` Viterbi for BIC selection is negligible (<1 % of a fit) — not adopted. New early-stop test; lint clean. Documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).
* **Burst — H2MM memory-bandwidth optimisations + unified engine selector.** The E-step is memory-bound, so two cache/bandwidth tricks (both numerically identical — A/B-vs-`H2MM_C` still exact): (1) **cache locality** — `α`/`scale` moved from a shared `(N, n)` array to small **per-thread scratch buffers** (sized to the longest burst, reused across bursts, hot in L1/L2), eliminating the largest DRAM stream. A **controlled isolated A/B** at 2.4M photons (one EM map) measures **1.25–1.6× on the E-step** (biggest at `n=3`), plus a *flat* ~10 ns/photon from 240k→2.4M (the old array caused a large-`N` cliff) and tens-of-MB lower peak memory. (2) **narrow integers** — `streams`→`int8`, `gap_slot`→`int16` (from `int32`): shrinks the index-array footprint ~3× but, once `α` is out of DRAM, is **speed-neutral** (isolated A/B 0.94–1.11×, within noise). **Correction:** an earlier note here claimed ~38 % from the int shrink at `n=2` — that was measurement noise on a loaded machine; the controlled A/B shows the cache-locality buffers are the real win and the int shrink is kept for footprint, not throughput. Confirmed SIMD is not worth a rewrite (state dim n=2–5 too small; over-burst SoA vectorisation eaten by memory bandwidth) and float32 already captures the easy width/bandwidth ~2×. Added a single **compute-engine selector** `core/engines.py` (`em`/`em-float32`/`surrogate`/`surrogate-refine`) threaded through `fit_states`(new `single_precision`)/`scan_states`/`analyze`; surrogate engines fall back to exact EM when no trained model is supplied, and model selection always scores by BIC/ICL. 19 burst_h2mm tests green; lint clean. New concept [PRD-60](/prds/prd-60.md); documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).

## 2026-07-08
* **Burst — H2MM Viterbi parallelised over bursts; state-splitting evaluated and rejected.** (a) `viterbi()` still ran a serial Python loop over bursts while the E-step was parallel; added `_viterbi_all` (a `prange` mirror — each burst decodes a disjoint `path[s:e]` with its own work arrays, path log-liks reduce), **≈3.2× faster** (6.8→2.1 ms on 300k photons, identical paths) and on the hot path of every model-selection scan (ICL) and final decode. (b) Tried warm-starting the multi-state scan by **state-splitting** the converged `(k-1)`-state fit (SMEM-style): empirically **unsafe** — a single split cannot undo the state merging in the smaller fit, so on well-separated 3-state data it reached a *worse* k=3 optimum (−251346 vs random −236009) yet a large gain-over-parent made naive "trust" heuristics accept it; the only safe variant (augment + always take best) is *slower*, not faster. Reverted the scan changes and removed the `split_model` helper; documented the negative result in `scan_states` and [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md). A robust version needs full split+merge SMEM (out of scope). **21 burst_h2mm tests green.**

Standalone **466 passed, 1 skipped**; auth suites green. Advances [PRD-59](/prds/prd-59.md).
* **Burst — H2MM engine: four compounding speedups (E-step fusion, SQUAREM, spectral build, float32).** Second optimisation pass on `core/h2mm.py`, each gated by the A/B-vs-`H2MM_C` tests. (1) **Two-pass E-step:** folded the γ (occupancy) and W (transition) accumulation into the single backward sweep and replaced the `(N, n)` β array with two `(n,)` vectors (β[n] needs only β[n+1]) — halving the large-array memory traffic; ~3–9 % faster (bigger at low `n`). (2) **SQUAREM acceleration** (`optimize(accelerate=True)`, default): squared-extrapolation EM (Varadhan & Roland 2008 S3) with a monotonicity safeguard reaching the *identical* fixed point in far fewer maps — 2-state **81→33** maps (2.4× faster), 3-state **807→132** (6× faster) on well-separated data. (3) **Spectral cache build** (`_build_caches_eig` + `_fill_caches`): for sparse photon streams (`n ≥ 3`, `max Δt ≥ 512`) `A^Δt`/`ρ` come from an eigendecomposition via divided differences instead of binary exponentiation (1.4–2.4× faster build at `max_dt≈2200`), conditioning-guarded with a pair-power fall-back; dense data keeps pair-power. (4) Opt-in **`single_precision`** float32 hot loop + caches (~1.9× at 3 states), explicitly approximate. Also fixed a latent landmine: ChiSurf's `env_bootstrap` rewrites `NUMBA_NUM_THREADS` *after* numba's pool launches, which crashed the first late cold compile (the float32 kernel) via numba's reload guard — `optimize` now re-pins the env to numba's launched pool size (`_sync_numba_threads`). New engine tests (SQUAREM≡plain-EM + fewer maps, eig≡pair-power build, eig declines on defective `A`, float32 near float64); **21 burst_h2mm tests green** (stable across repeated full-dir runs). Net vs `H2MM_C` on the slow benchmark: **0.51×** (2-state) / **0.52×** (3-state) wall-time per map, now also converging in fewer maps. Documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).
* **Burst — H2MM A/B *performance* guard vs `H2MM_C`.** Added `test_benchmark_vs_reference` (2- and 3-state) to `tests/test_ab_vs_h2mm_c.py` as a companion to the correctness A/B tests: it times a full EM run of the numba port against the reference C `H2MM_C` on identical tttrlib-simulated data, reports **ms/EM-iteration** (JIT warmed up first, so compilation isn't charged; normalised per iteration so convergence-count differences don't skew it), and asserts (a) the two engines reach the same optimum and (b) the port stays under ~1.5× the reference time/iter — a wide-margin regression guard that would catch an `O(N·n⁴)`-style slowdown. Marked `slow` (excluded from default runs; run with `-m slow -s`). Measured on 150k-photon dense bursts: **0.68×** (2-state) / **0.50×** (3-state) the `H2MM_C` wall-time per iteration. Documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).
* **Burst — H2MM E-step now beats the reference `H2MM_C` (defer the ρ contraction).** The parallel E-step (`core/h2mm.py::_estep`) formed the transition tensor ξ *per gap* — an `O(N·n⁴)` inner loop that also streamed the whole `rho_cache` from memory once per photon — leaving the numba engine ~1.05–1.21× *slower* than `H2MM_C` (gap widening with `n_states`). Restructured to accumulate only the per-unique-Δt weight `W[slot,k,m] = Σ_gaps α[n,k]·obs[m,y_{n+1}]·β[n+1,m]/c` in the hot loop (`O(N·n²)`, thread-local), then contract `ξ[i,j] = Σ_{slot,k,m} W[slot,k,m]·ρ[slot,k,m,i,j]` **once per slot** in the serial reduction (`O(n_slots·n⁴)`, `n_slots` = unique inter-photon Δt ≪ N). Mathematically identical (ρ is fixed per slot, so the per-gap sum factors out); `rho_cache` is now read `n_slots` times instead of N. On 2000×120-photon simulated data (100 EM iters) the engine went from ~1.05×/0.95×/1.12× the `H2MM_C` wall-time at 2/3/4 states to **0.61×/0.37×/0.28×** — i.e. ~1.6×/2.7×/3.6× *faster*; the 4-state fit dropped 1253→334 ms. All 10 A/B-vs-`H2MM_C` + engine tests still green (converged logL/BIC/params and Viterbi match the reference to the same tolerances). Documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).
* **MMFDB — threaded + enforced `auth` across the whole `api.py` boundary (INC-04).** Most `api.py` functions ran unauthenticated and lacked an `auth` parameter — yet **all ~40 are registered as `mmfdb.v1.*` RPCs invoked via `h(**params, auth=auth)`**, so those versioned methods would have `TypeError`'d the moment they were called with a token: a latent break *and* the enforcement gap. Added `auth` to every one (samples/experiments/operations/parameters/graph/setups/chinet/branches/audit) with shared helpers for **progressive enforcement**: `_acting_user_id` (authenticated principal, else configured default — preserves in-process/GUI), `_new_object_acl` (writes stamp the owner + a default ACL: samples/experiments join the existing artifact/operation ACLs), `_acl_read_or_pass`/`_acl_filter_or_pass` (reads enforce ACLs *where they exist*, stay open otherwise — no legacy lockout), and `_effective_target_user` making the user-scoped branch ops **self-or-admin** (fixed an IDOR where any user could set/read another's active branch). New `tests/test_api_auth.py` (5: auth accepted + owner-ACL + cross-user filtering, graceful no-ACL reads, in-process default-user attribution, IDOR blocked, admin-may-target-other). Standalone **468 passed, 1 skipped** (was 463); `test/fio` **236 passed** (1 pre-existing). Marked [INC-04](/specs/assessment.md#inc-04) 🚧 ADDRESSED. (Landed alongside a concurrent `mmfdb.admin`→`mmfdb_admin` extraction in the tree; committed only the `api.py`/test changes.)
* **Burst — new H2MM photon-by-photon HMM plugin (`burst_h2mm`).** Added a single-molecule FRET plugin that resolves sub-burst state dynamics on the microsecond scale, ported from the Pirchi *et al.* 2016 / `H2MM_C` algorithm into a **self-contained numba engine** (no external H2MM dependency). `core/h2mm.py` caches `A^Δt` and the transition-count `ρ` tensor once per **unique** inter-photon Δt via associative pair-power binary exponentiation (cost scales with photons, not clock ticks), runs a scaled forward-backward + Baum-Welch EM, and provides Viterbi+ICL, BIC, a model factory and a validation simulator. Follows the client-server standard: Qt-free `core/` (h2mm/photons/analysis) → RPC `backend/services.py` (`burst_h2mm.jobs.compute`) → thin `H2mmClient` + `H2mmTool` GUI (FRET states, transition-density plot, BIC/ICL model selection, per-state dwell-time distributions) + click CLI. Consumes `.bur` bursts sliced from `tttrlib.TTTR`, mapping routing-channel + micro-time windows to photon streams. Wired into `burst_analysis` as **step 6 "H2MM"** with workflow-context handoff (inherits burst folder + channel defs). Marked **experimental** (numba engine validated on simulated ground-truth recovery, monotonic logL, BIC selection, Viterbi, RPC, stream-gating, headless GUI). **A/B-verified numerically equivalent to the reference `H2MM_C`** on tttrlib-simulated data carried through the real `tttrlib.TTTR` + plugin extraction path: fixed-model and converged log-likelihood/BIC agree to ~1e-9, π/trans/obs to ~1e-7 (2- and 3-state), and Viterbi paths match 100% over ~36k photons (`tests/test_ab_vs_h2mm_c.py`, skips if `H2MM_C` absent). 15 tests green; not yet validated on experimental data. Documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).
* **MMFDB Admin boundary correction — API/CLI stay in `mmfdb.admin`, GUI split to `mmfdb-admin`.** Corrected the prerelease admin ownership line: `mmfdb.admin` remains the admin API/CLI package (RPC service implementation, direct in-process API client, CLI/`mmfdb-admin` console script), while the former ChiSurf plugin GUI now lives in sibling package `modules/mmfdb-admin` as the standalone `mmfdb-admin-gui` Qt surface. The ChiSurf `core/mmfdb_admin` plugin is now a shim: manifest services point to `mmfdb.admin.backend.services`, and GUI construction delegates to `mmfdb_admin.gui.app`. Ported a ChiSurf-free AutoForm layer into `mmfdb-admin` and wired browse tabs to AutoForm-backed row detail panes. Added boundary coverage for the split and smoke-verified standalone CLI status plus offscreen GUI construction.
* **MMFDB — auth polish: external-user password guard + auth-services lint cleanup (PRD-59).** Rounding out the auth layer: `change_password` (both the token-based `auth_services.change_password_handler` and the legacy `password_services.change_password_handler`) now **rejects external-provider users** — their credential lives in the directory/IdP, so writing a local hash was meaningless (and confusing). Cleaned the pre-existing lint debt in `auth_services.py` (9 → 0), including a **real latent bug** — the `require_handler_auth` return annotation referenced undefined `sqlite3`/`Principal` (F821; harmless only because `from __future__ import annotations` stringifies it) — plus removed 5 genuinely-unused re-imports (verified nothing imports them from that module) and sorted imports; same for `password_services.py`. 1 new regression test. Deliberately **not** done (low value, noted): user-enumeration timing equalization on the local path — network jitter dominates PBKDF2 timing and MMFDB isn't internet-facing.
* **MMFDB — closed a critical auth hole + enforced "local always available" (PRD-59 security review).** Auditing "what else needs doing," found that an **external (LDAP) user could be logged in via the local provider with an empty password**: JIT-provisioned directory users have no local `password_hash`, and `LocalAuthProvider`'s (and legacy `password_services.login_handler`'s) "no hash → accept when no password" branch treated them as passwordless — `login(provider="local", user_id="<ldap_uid>", password="")` succeeded without the directory. Fixed by making **both** local-auth paths reject users whose `auth_provider != 'local'` (genuine local passwordless users are unaffected). Also found a **lockout risk**: with LDAP as the configured default, the bootstrap **local admin couldn't log in** (default dispatch sent everyone to LDAP). Added a **local fallback** in `login()` — when a non-local default returns `None`, the local provider is tried — making "Local always available" real; it can't weaken security because the local provider now rejects external-homed users (a directory-rejected external user still fails). Third finding: **email-match could hijack a real local account** — an LDAP user whose email collides with an existing local admin was silently relinked (`auth_provider→ldap`), handing control to whoever holds that directory account. Now `resolve_or_provision_user` only email-adopts a **placeholder** local account (local-homed, no password); a real local-credential or other-provider account is never converted (JIT mints a distinct account instead). 4 new regression tests (external-user local-login blocked incl. empty password; local admin logs in under LDAP-default; external user can't sneak through the fallback; email collision doesn't hijack a local password account). Standalone **461 passed, 1 skipped** (was 457); `test/fio` **236 passed** (1 pre-existing).
* **MMFDB — auth hardening + extensible provider registry (PRD-59 Phase 4).** Made the auth layer excellent + extensible (per the "great arch, extend later" directive). **Provider registry** (`register_provider`/`build_provider`/`available_providers` + `ProviderContext` in `security/auth_providers.py`): the sole extension point — a new backend (OIDC, external-IdP, …) is a class + one registration call; `login.resolve_provider` now dispatches through it and never needs editing (built-in `local`/`ldap` self-register). **Fixed a real security bug:** failed RPC logins weren't persisted (each `login_handler` opens its own connection and the old flow raised without committing), so `is_throttled` never accumulated and brute-force throttling was silently disabled — `login._record_failure` now commits the attempt (empirically 0→≥5 persisted across connections). **Directory-authoritative reconciliation** (`sync_identity`): external-provider logins refresh `is_admin`/`email`/`display_name` and reconcile the provider's new `AuthIdentity.managed_groups` (add carried, remove absent; admin membership follows `is_admin`) while never touching locally-managed groups. **LDAP hardened:** `base_dn` validation, `try/finally` unbind, optional TLS CA (`ca_cert`→`ldap3.Tls`), and unreachable/search errors → clear `AuthError` (wrong password stays `None`). New `tests/test_auth_hardening.py` (9: registry extend/build/unknown, throttle-persists-across-RPC-connections, attribute+group reconciliation incl. de-escalation and unmanaged-group safety, LDAP missing-base-dn / directory-unavailable / managed-groups). Wrote the **PRD-59** concept (`okf/prds/prd-59.md`, status in-progress) + index/glyph and an auth-provider section in `okf/architecture/mmfdb.md`. **Correction:** Phase-1/2 log bullets and code docstrings mislabelled this work "PRD-49" (which is the unrelated Multiparameter-Fluorescence PRD); renumbered to the next free id **PRD-59** across code/tests/log (Phase-1/2 commit *messages* keep the old label — history). New `tests/test_ldap_auth.py` (10 tests via MOCK_SYNC: attr+group mapping, wrong/empty password, unknown user, service-bind-failure → `AuthError`, filter-injection escaping, missing-dep `ImportError`, `login()` JIT-provision + group-sync end-to-end, and the env/resolver config path). ## 2026-07-07
* **MMFDB — eliminated the last `INSERT OR REPLACE` in `repository.py` + `analysis_data`; the package is now `INSERT OR REPLACE`-free (PRD-26).** With `dao.upsert` keyless-tolerant, converted the remaining 11 `INSERT OR REPLACE` writes in the repository core + the `analysis_data` one, choosing the target per table's actual constraint: **real conflict target → `dao.upsert`** — `add_vocabulary` (`field_name,value`), `set_experiment_key_value` (`experiment_id,key`), `add_optical_property` (`probe_id,property_name`), `add_photon_stream` (`stream_id`), `add_analysis_data` (`analysis_id,data_type,data_name`, keeping the load-bearing soft-delete UPDATE that dedups the NULL-`data_name` case SQLite's UNIQUE treats as distinct); **autoincrement-id / no-UNIQUE → `dao.insert`** — `add_chemical_descriptor`, `add_image`, and `add_external_file` (always-fresh uuid, so its follow-up `SELECT id` collapsed into the `insert` return). **A real finding:** `citeulike`, `products`, `standards`, `product_categories` have **neither a PK nor a UNIQUE** in the reconciled schema, so their `INSERT OR REPLACE` was silently a plain insert (duplicate ids possible) — converted to `dao.insert` with a comment making the missing-constraint gap explicit rather than pretending to upsert (a real fix needs a schema PK; noted for follow-up). Standalone **421 passed, 1 skipped**; `test/fio` **236 passed** (1 pre-existing). Audit: insert 64 → 53 (repository.py 13 → 2, its only raw inserts now the append-only `mmfdb_parameter`/`mmfdb_audit_log` core). **No `INSERT OR REPLACE` remains anywhere in the package.** Advances [PRD-26](/prds/prd-26.md)/[INC-05](/specs/assessment.md#inc-05).
* **MMFDB — made `dao.upsert` keyless-tolerant; converted the last "keyless-table" `INSERT OR REPLACE` writes (PRD-26).** Root-caused the documented "keyless tables can't be upserted" limitation: `analysis_metadata` and `flr_sample_key_value` have **no PRIMARY KEY but a real `UNIQUE(…, key)`** constraint, so they *are* valid `ON CONFLICT` targets — the only blocker was `dao.upsert` calling `primary_key()` *unconditionally* at the end (to pick a return value), which raised `DaoError` before the caller's explicit `conflict` could help. Wrapped that in `try/except DaoError → return lastrowid`, mirroring the same fix already in `dao.insert`. With that, converted the three surviving `INSERT OR REPLACE` writes onto identity-preserving upserts: `SampleMixin.set_sample_key_value` (`conflict=["sample_id","key"]`) and `AnalysisMixin.add_analysis_metadata` + the `set_analysis_metadata` reseed loop (`conflict=["analysis_id","key"]`) — re-add now clears `deleted_at` in place instead of delete-and-reinsert. Added `test_upsert_into_keyless_table_on_unique` (sibling to the keyless-`insert` test). Standalone suite **421 passed, 1 skipped**. Audit: insert 67 → 64. **`flr_sample_key_value`/`analysis_metadata` are no longer a DAO limitation** — the only genuinely un-upsertable tables left are those with *neither* a PK *nor* a targetable UNIQUE. Advances [PRD-26](/prds/prd-26.md)/[INC-05](/specs/assessment.md#inc-05).
* **MMFDB — swept the trivial single-table SELECTs in `queries/*.py` onto the DAO (PRD-26).** With the scattered-CRUD migration complete, converted the *trivial* reads in the centralized query mixins — single-table select-by-PK and equality-filter reads → `db.dao.get`/`db.dao.list` — across all 13 query files (users, parameters, experiments, branches, protocols, samples, studies, analysis, setups, probes, artifacts; objects/lifecycle had none convertible). Also folded a handful of coupled raw writes that a SELECT hung off (e.g. `add_experiment_data`'s `INSERT`+`last_insert_rowid()` → `dao.insert`). **Deliberately left raw** (the legitimate centralized home): JOINs, `DISTINCT`/`COUNT`/`MAX` aggregates, `LIKE` search, `json_extract` filters, `IN (…)`/`OR` predicates, `sqlite_master`/`PRAGMA` introspection, subquery/latest-per-group, compound `ORDER BY` (the DAO's `list` is single-column), reads on the external source `spectra.db` connection, and the `consolidate_probes` merge (dynamic `probe_id`/`item_id` key columns). **Lessons that shaped the sweep:** (1) `dao.get` needs an explicit `pk_column` when the dictionary schema doesn't mark the PK and the `<table>_id`/`id`/`uuid` fallback misses (`mmfdb_protocol.protocol_id`, `mmfdb_study.study_id`, `spectra.spectrum_id` — the last has a *separate* autoincrement `id`, so the fallback would silently query the wrong column); (2) `dao.list`/`get` return plain dicts, so any caller doing positional `row[0]`/tuple-unpacking had to be checked first (only `studies.backfill` and a couple of projections kept their raw form for that reason); (3) reads with **no** `deleted_at` guard were preserved with `include_deleted=True`; (4) converting `find_or_add_probe`'s refetch to a dict incidentally fixed a latent `sqlite3.Row.get()` call. Verified after every file — standalone **420 passed, 1 skipped** throughout; `test/fio` **236 passed** (1 pre-existing `ndxplorer` fail). Audit: select **241 → 175**; `probes.py` reads reclassified into bespoke (JOIN/aggregate/source/merge), so bespoke rose 68 → 87 as an accuracy correction, not new raw SQL. This was the optional item-3 cleanup in `HANDOVER.md`; the remaining `queries/` SELECTs are all the sanctioned bespoke home. Advances [PRD-26](/prds/prd-26.md)/[INC-05](/specs/assessment.md#inc-05).
* **MMFDB — converted the last `INSERT OR REPLACE` in `queries/` (`add_operation_artifact`) to a composite-PK upsert (PRD-26).** The earlier "clear the remaining `INSERT OR REPLACE`/`IGNORE` in `queries/`" pass had left `ArtifactOpsMixin.add_operation_artifact` raw because `mmfdb_operation_artifact`'s 4-column composite PK was believed un-targetable by the DAO. Having disproven that (see the `seed_example` bullet below), routed it onto `db.dao.upsert(conflict=["operation_id","artifact_id","direction","role"])` — the `role`/`direction` are conflict columns and `created_at`/`updated_at`/`deleted_at` are the update set, so on re-add it refreshes the timestamps and **resurrects** a soft-deleted link (`deleted_at → NULL`) in place, identity-preserving where `INSERT OR REPLACE` would delete-and-reinsert. Verified the insert / soft-delete / re-add cycle keeps a single row with `deleted_at=NULL`. The two `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO mmfdb_group_member` writes in `schema.py`'s `bootstrap_*` stay `# raw` — they run on a **bare `sqlite3.Connection`** with no `dao` in scope (the documented bootstrap-seeder pattern). Standalone suite **420 passed, 1 skipped**. Audit: `queries/artifacts.py` insert 6 → 5; total insert 69 → 68. Advances [PRD-26](/prds/prd-26.md)/[INC-05](/specs/assessment.md#inc-05).
* **MMFDB — routed the demo seeder `admin/seed_example.py` through the DAO (PRD-26 burn-down).** The example-smFRET seeder is the last non-query module carrying scattered CRUD; it holds an `MFDatabase` handle throughout, so `db.dao` is in scope. Converted every existence-check-then-insert helper: the probe/experiment-type/poly-probe-position lookups (`SELECT … WHERE <non-PK/UNIQUE>` → `db.dao.list(filters=…, limit=1)`), the user/device/entity/assembly/condition/artifact/operation existence probes (`SELECT 1 WHERE <pk>` → `db.dao.get(...) is None`), and the raw inserts for `entities` + `entity_poly_seq`, `flr_entity_assembly`, `flr_sample_condition`, and `flr_poly_probe_position` → `db.dao.insert` (the last returning the autoincrement `id` via lastrowid). The `probe_types` `INSERT OR IGNORE`+SELECT-back collapsed into `dao.upsert(conflict=["type_name"])` + `dao.list`. **Correction to a documented "DAO limitation":** the two `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO mmfdb_operation_artifact` writes on the **4-column composite-PK junction** also went onto the DAO — `dao.upsert(conflict=["operation_id","artifact_id","direction","role"])` targets the full composite PK, and since the values *are* exactly those 4 columns the upsert is an idempotent `DO NOTHING` (identity-preserving, unlike the delete-and-reinsert of `INSERT OR REPLACE`). So `seed_example.py` is now **zero raw SQL**; composite-PK junctions are convertible whenever you can name the full PK as the conflict target (only *keyless* tables with no targetable UNIQUE remain a genuine limitation). ## 2026-07-06
* **MMFDB — god-class breakup: `repository.py` 6,397 → 1,848 lines (−71%).** Resumed and largely completed the Phase-4 [PRD-26](/prds/prd-26.md)/[INC-05](/specs/assessment.md#inc-05) decomposition of the `MFDatabase` god-class into per-concern query mixins under `queries/`. Extracted six new mixins this pass — **ProbeMixin** (probe/spectra/optical/Förster), **SampleMixin** (samples/entities/positions/linkage), **SetupCalibMixin** (setups/calibrations), **ObjectStoreMixin** (object store + materialization), **ArtifactOpsMixin** (the artifact/operation/edge/provenance-graph core, ~46 methods), and **AnalysisMixin** (analysis runs/products/metadata) — for **13 mixins** total. Built a reusable AST-boundary method extractor (handles multi-line signatures, decorators, and leaves class attributes in place); relocated module-level helpers (`_default_reference_spectra_path`→`store/database_resolver`, `_validate_checksum`→`schema/_sqlutil`) to avoid repository↔mixin import cycles, and carried class-level method aliases (`save_setup_snapshot`, `link_operation_artifact`) into their mixins. Public `MFDatabase` surface unchanged (methods resolve via the MRO); standalone suite **419 passed** after every extraction. `repository.py` is now a thin composition over `self.conn`/`self.dao`/`self.lineage` — what remains is the legitimate core (init/connection/properties, migration, audit, vocabulary, experiment key-values, pdbx metadata).
* **MMFDB — admin GUI moved out; `adapters/` subpackage added.** Continued the clean-bounds migration: relocated the chisurf-coupled admin **GUI** (24 modules + 7 view-spec JSONs) out of the package into the ChiSurf plugin (`chisurf/plugins/core/mmfdb_admin/gui/`), replacing the compat wrappers and retargeting 38 importers + the manifest entrypoint; the admin **backend** (RPC handlers) stays in `mmfdb.admin` and is chisurf-free. Added an **`adapters/`** subpackage as the home for external-system bridges — moved `chinet_adapter` → `mmfdb.adapters.chinet` (ChiSurf fit sessions → MMFDB), with eLabFTW / electronic-lab-notebook adapters to follow; adapters keep target-system imports lazy so the core still imports standalone. Top-level `mmfdb` is now 5 files. Standalone: 419 passed. Advances [PRD-24](/prds/prd-24.md)/[PRD-48](/prds/prd-48.md).
* **MMFDB — own hermetic test suite + concern-subpackage reorg (PRD-24).** Gave the package clear bounds and a maintainable file layout. (1) **Relocated ~35 pure-MMFDB test modules** from ChiSurf `test/fio`+`test/plugins` into `modules/mmfdb/tests/` with a hermetic conftest (isolation via MMFDB's own `MMFDB_SETTINGS_DIR`, no chisurf import); the suite runs standalone (`cd modules/mmfdb && PYTHONPATH=src pytest`). This immediately exposed **real boundary violations** in the package — fixed the module-level ones (`admin/backend/services` used `from chisurf import logging` → stdlib; `{measurement,ndxplorer}_services` imported `chisurf.server.services` error helpers → new `mmfdb.admin.backend._service_errors`). ChiSurf↔MMFDB integration tests (admin GUI `MMFDBClient`, chinet/`parameter_registry` alignment, ndxplorer submodule, chisurf test-data) stay in the ChiSurf tree. (2) **Reorganized the 38 flat top-level modules into concern subpackages** — `schema/ store/ provenance/ samples/ lifecycle/ security/ project/` — leaving 6 core files at top (`repository`, `api`, `models`, `config`, `chinet_adapter`, `__init__`); collapsed the `auth/`-only-`__init__` "package" to `auth.py`. Hard cutover (no compat shims): every internal, test, and ChiSurf import retargeted to grouped paths (`mmfdb.schema.dao`, `mmfdb.provenance.result_registry`, …); fixed `Path(__file__).parent/"data"` resolution in the seven moved modules that read bundled data. **Proof of clean bounds: 419 passed with only `src` on the path** (no chisurf, no chinet). ChiSurf `test/fio`: 236 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`test_ndxplorer_cli`, needs the ndxplorer submodule). Advances [PRD-24](/prds/prd-24.md); layout documented in [architecture/mmfdb.md](/architecture/mmfdb.md).
* **MMFDB — reimplemented external-reference persistence (PRD-39); test/fio 7 → 1.** The struct_ref/external-reference write path was lost when the SQLAlchemy `orm/` stack was deleted (Merge 1) and never reproduced on the raw-SQL path — `create_sample` recorded entities but silently dropped their UniProt/PDB cross-references and mutations. Reimplemented minimally: `sample_manager._persist_entity_external_refs` records `uniprot_accession`→`struct_ref(db_name=UNP)`, `pdb_id`→`struct_ref(db_name=PDB)`, the primary reference's sequence alignment as `struct_ref_seq`, and engineered mutations (given, or auto-diffed from `reference_sequence` via `external_refs.diff_sequences`) as `struct_ref_seq_dif`; `get_sample_full_description` now surfaces per-entity `external_refs`/`mutations`, and the probe↔mutation export validator resolves the entity via the position's `entity_id` (added to the read) with a `residue_number`/`residue_name` fallback for `seq_id`/`comp_id`. **Writes go through the dictionary-driven `DictionaryDao` (`db.dao.insert`/`list`), not hand SQL** — and codified that: raw/f-string SQL for CRUD is now documented as an **antipattern** in [architecture/mmfdb.md](/architecture/mmfdb.md) (one engine = `db.dao`; raw SQL only for bespoke joins/graph/aggregate reads). Also fixed a latent `_array_to_text` `TypeError` (np.frombuffer on a text blob) in the flrCIF export path. `test/fio` now **656 passed / 1 failed**; the lone remaining failure (`test_ndxplorer_cli`) is an out-of-scope environment issue (needs the `ndxplorer` submodule built). Advances [PRD-19](/prds/prd-19.md)/[PRD-26](/prds/prd-26.md)/[INC-05](/specs/assessment.md#inc-05).
* **MMFDB simplification — post-cutover stabilization: test/fio 179 → 7 failures.** The Merge-3 cutover exposed a broken full suite; root-caused and fixed it in committed batches. **The dominant cause (~150 cascading failures) was a single global-state leak:** `test_fcs_setup.py`'s v36-migration test set the module global `schema.SCHEMA_VERSION = 35` and never restored it, so every later test's fresh `MFDatabase` skipped the version-40 reconcile-to-`.dic` step and came up with a partial schema (missing `mmfdb_state_transition`, `mmfdb_operation.protocol_id`). Removed that obsolete test (no v36 migration exists after the PRD-19 collapse to `MIGRATIONS={1,40}`). Then fixed the independent failures: a **live default-user-id bridge** ([PRD-24](/prds/prd-24.md)) — `mmfdb.config.set_default_user_id_resolver` consulted by `configured_default_user_id`, registered from `chisurf.core.settings` to read `cs_settings` on each call (MMFDB stays standalone); a real **`get_parameter` bug** (delegated to `dao.get` on the table PK `parameter_id` instead of the `parameter_uuid` column → always None); `importer.py` `get_probe_by_id`→`get_probe`; `migrate_schema` returns no report for a fresh (from-scratch) database; and a batch of stale-reference test fixes after the cutover (flr_ext `.dic` via `MmcifDictionary.DATA_DIR`, `python -m mmfdb.pdbx_metadata`, `mmfdb.admin.backend.services`, admin session-token minting now that a fresh DB seeds a `user_default` admin, stale `get_optical_properties`/`get_spectrum` shapes, explicit plugin-manifest path). **Remaining 7:** `test_external_refs` (6) is a real **PRD-39 feature reimplementation** — struct_ref/external-reference persistence (uniprot/pdb→`struct_ref`, mutations→`struct_ref_seq_dif`, sequence auto-diff, export validation, and surfacing `external_refs`/`mutations` in `get_sample_full_description`) was lost when the SQLAlchemy `orm/` stack was deleted in Merge 1 and never reimplemented on the raw-SQL path; `test_ndxplorer_cli` (1) is an out-of-scope environment issue (needs the `ndxplorer` submodule built). Advances [INC-05](/specs/assessment.md#inc-05)/[PRD-24](/prds/prd-24.md).
* **MMFDB simplification — Merge 3 cutover landed: one import namespace, dead shim gone.** Committed the previously-uncommitted cutover in three coherent local commits. (1) Deleted the shadowed `chisurf/core/mmfdb/*.py` shim modules — the facade `__init__.py` already routes `chisurf.core.mmfdb.X → mmfdb.X` via its meta-path `_AliasFinder`, so the sibling real files were duplicate shadows whose presence broke test isolation (two `database_resolver`/event-bus copies); kept the thin facade + `auth/` + `data/`. (2) Repointed the `mmfdb_admin` plugin at the relocated `mmfdb.admin.*` package (manifest entrypoints + backend/GUI compat wrappers) and deleted the retired `sample_database` plugin. (3) Fixed a bad find-replace from the cutover that had rewritten five test modules' admin Python import paths `mmfdb_admin → mmfdb.admin`, producing the nonexistent hybrid `chisurf.plugins.core.mmfdb.admin.*` and a hard `ModuleNotFoundError` (the "3 stale reds" flagged in the Merge-1 note, actually 5) — repointed to canonical `mmfdb.admin.*`, unblocking 136 tests. Net effect: clean-HEAD `test/fio` went from **660 collection errors** (duplicate-module chaos) to a runnable suite; mmfdb-core gate still 161 passed. **Newly exposed** by the now-running suite: ~163 `test/fio` failures across three root causes — global-state test-ordering leaks, `cs_settings`-not-flowing-into-standalone-`mmfdb.config` decoupling (PRD-24, deferred), and a stale hardcoded `CREATE_TABLES_SQL` (`mmfdb_operation` missing `protocol_id`/`protocol_version` vs the canonical `_TableDef`, Phase 3). * **MMFDB simplification — Merge 2 in progress: god-class breakup begun.** Added identity-preserving `DictionaryDao.upsert` (INSERT…ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE — the safe write path the `add_*`/`save_*` family re-roots onto). Extracted pure JSON/time helpers into `mmfdb/_sqlutil.py` (breaks the import cycle mixins would form). Splitting the 7,322-line `MFDatabase` god-class into per-concern mixins under `mmfdb/queries/`: **ParameterMixin, StudyMixin, ProtocolMixin, LifecycleMixin, BranchMixin, UserDeviceMixin, ExperimentMixin** (7 concerns; public method surface unchanged — methods resolve via MRO, zero delegators); `repository.py` 7,322 → 6,389 lines.
