* **Burst — H2MM plugin polish: engine select, defined ndX output, CLI/GUI, notebook, docs.** Rounded the H2MM plugin into a finished tool. **Engine selection** end-to-end: `H2mmSettings` gains `engine`/`refine_iters`/`patience`/`surrogate_path`/`write_photons`; the GUI settings tab has an engine dropdown + scan-patience spinner, the `h2mm compute` CLI has `--engine`/`--surrogate`/`--patience`/`--refine-iters`/`--no-photons`, and both flow through `analyze`. **Defined output openable in ndxplorer**: `core/export.py` builds a **per-photon** table (Viterbi `State` + macro/micro time, channel, stream) and a **per-burst** summary, written as `<folder>/h2mm/h2mm_photons.h5` (pandas key `results`) + `h2mm_bursts.csv` — plain numeric tables with a `Mean Macro Time (s)` axis that ndX opens directly; `photons.py` extended with `PhotonMeta` + `return_meta` so per-photon macro/micro/channel align with the engine layout. **Notebook** `examples/notebooks/H2MM_01_Simulated_smFRET.ipynb` (linear, matplotlib, no `__main__`): simulate smFRET via `tttrlib` → extract → fit/select → Viterbi trajectory → engine comparison → ndX export; validated end-to-end via `nbconvert --execute`. **Docs** `docs/H2MM.md` (theory: photon-by-photon HMM, the `A^Δt` variable-Δt trick, Baum-Welch, BIC/ICL, Viterbi; engines; outputs; CLI/API) registered in `docs/index.rst`. New `tests/test_export.py` (meta alignment, table schema/numeric-only, HDF5/CSV round-trip). **30 burst_h2mm tests green** (incl. GUI instantiation with the new dropdown); lint clean.
* **Burst — H2MM model-selection early-stopping + SIMD/scan-trick dead-ends recorded.** Explored further *algorithmic* speed-ups now that per-fit exact EM is at the roofline. (1) **Early-stop the state-count scan** (`scan_states`/`analyze` opt-in `patience`): the BIC/ICL curve is U-shaped and the over-fit high-`k` fits are the *most expensive* — a redundant state makes a flat likelihood ridge so they run to `max_iter` without converging (measured: k=1..5 on 2-state data took 5/24/500/500/500 maps). Stopping once the criterion has risen for `patience+1` counts gave a **measured 1.65× faster scan** with identical selection; `patience=None` (default) is unchanged. (2) **SIMD confirmed a dead end by experiment:** reordering the forward matmul from a `k`-reduction to a supposedly-SIMD-friendly `i`-inner AXPY made it **0.3–0.7× (slower)** at n=2..5 — LLVM already register-optimises the small unrolled reduction, and over-burst SoA batching is structurally blocked by H2MM's variable-Δt design (each burst/photon needs a *different* transition matrix → per-lane gather, no uniform SIMD op). Not adopted. (3) Skipping per-`k` Viterbi for BIC selection is negligible (<1 % of a fit) — not adopted. New early-stop test; lint clean. Documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).
* **Burst — H2MM memory-bandwidth optimisations + unified engine selector.** The E-step is memory-bound, so two cache/bandwidth tricks (both numerically identical — A/B-vs-`H2MM_C` still exact): (1) **cache locality** — `α`/`scale` moved from a shared `(N, n)` array to small **per-thread scratch buffers** (sized to the longest burst, reused across bursts, hot in L1/L2), eliminating the largest DRAM stream. A **controlled isolated A/B** at 2.4M photons (one EM map) measures **1.25–1.6× on the E-step** (biggest at `n=3`), plus a *flat* ~10 ns/photon from 240k→2.4M (the old array caused a large-`N` cliff) and tens-of-MB lower peak memory. (2) **narrow integers** — `streams`→`int8`, `gap_slot`→`int16` (from `int32`): shrinks the index-array footprint ~3× but, once `α` is out of DRAM, is **speed-neutral** (isolated A/B 0.94–1.11×, within noise). **Correction:** an earlier note here claimed ~38 % from the int shrink at `n=2` — that was measurement noise on a loaded machine; the controlled A/B shows the cache-locality buffers are the real win and the int shrink is kept for footprint, not throughput. Confirmed SIMD is not worth a rewrite (state dim n=2–5 too small; over-burst SoA vectorisation eaten by memory bandwidth) and float32 already captures the easy width/bandwidth ~2×. Added a single **compute-engine selector** `core/engines.py` (`em`/`em-float32`/`surrogate`/`surrogate-refine`) threaded through `fit_states`(new `single_precision`)/`scan_states`/`analyze`; surrogate engines fall back to exact EM when no trained model is supplied, and model selection always scores by BIC/ICL. 19 burst_h2mm tests green; lint clean. (CLI/GUI engine wiring, ndX-openable per-photon output, notebook + docs still to land.) Documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).
* **Burst — optional amortised (surrogate) neural estimator for H2MM (PRD-60, draft).** After proving the remaining H2MM speed-up can only come from cutting EM's iteration count — and that *initialisation can't do it* (seeding Baum-Welch from the exact generative parameters still took ~39 maps vs ~42 random; only starting from the dataset's own MLE hit the ~6-map floor, because EM's cost is the finite-sample last mile) — added a **simulation-based-inference** fast path that *replaces* EM: `core/surrogate.py` trains a small scikit-learn MLP once on simulator draws to predict `(prior, trans, obs)` in one forward pass. POC: on held-out 2-state data the surrogate recovered per-state FRET to **0.028–0.032** mean-abs-error vs **0.047–0.052** for a single EM fit (more accurate — it's a Bayes estimator under the training prior — and faster, the gap widening with N). Module is Qt-free, `numpy`+`scikit-learn` only (already a dep), permutation-invariant features (windowed-FRET histogram/quantiles + photon-lag autocorrelation + Δt stats, versioned), canonical-ordered/`log10`-transition encoding, fast O(photons) training simulator, `save`/`load`, and an optional `refine_iters` EM polish. Wired as opt-in `fit_states(surrogate=…, refine_iters=…)` (default `None` → EM unchanged); ships **disabled, no pretrained model**, EM fallback when scikit-learn absent. Approximate — for over-determined data/exploration, not final numbers or model selection. Also concluded (measured) that GPU offload is a dead end here: on the M1 Pro, jax-metal couldn't compile the forward-backward `lax.scan`, and a single Metal batched-matmul step (0.786 ms) already ≈ numba's entire 240k-photon forward — the tiny-state sequential recurrence can't use a GPU. 5 surrogate tests; **26 burst_h2mm tests green**. New concept [PRD-60](/prds/prd-60.md); documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).
* **MMFDB — metadata→edge materialization + resolvable audit labels (ELN crosslinking lessons).** Studied a mature ELN's information-management/crosslinking model and adopted two provenance-integrity wins. (1) A sample/experiment key-value whose value is an `mmfdb://<node_type>/<node_id>` reference now **materializes an idempotent `mmfdb_edge`** (`linked_to`, tagged with the originating metadata key) from the owning node to the referenced node — the ELN pattern "a metadata field that references another entity *is* a link" (`queries/artifacts.py::parse_node_ref`/`_materialize_metadata_ref`, wired into `set_sample_key_value`/`set_experiment_key_value`). (2) Edge/link creation audit entries (`add_edge`, `record_operation_link`) now carry a **resolvable target label** (the node's human title via `_resolve_node_label`), mirroring the ELN's changelog anchors. New `tests/test_metadata_edges.py` (5). Confirmed MMFDB's single polymorphic `mmfdb_edge` is architecturally ahead of the ELN's ~25-table per-pair junction matrix (do not copy it), and its `.dic`-driven vocab beats freeform extra_fields for a databank. Deferred as an **idea for later**: an optional polymorphic **tags** layer (scoped, AND-searchable) — recorded in [ELN crosslinking lessons](/references/eln-crosslinking-lessons.md). Standalone **471 passed, 1 skipped**; `test/fio` **236 passed** (1 pre-existing).

## 2026-07-08
* **Burst — H2MM Viterbi parallelised over bursts; state-splitting evaluated and rejected.** (a) `viterbi()` still ran a serial Python loop over bursts while the E-step was parallel; added `_viterbi_all` (a `prange` mirror — each burst decodes a disjoint `path[s:e]` with its own work arrays, path log-liks reduce), **≈3.2× faster** (6.8→2.1 ms on 300k photons, identical paths) and on the hot path of every model-selection scan (ICL) and final decode. (b) Tried warm-starting the multi-state scan by **state-splitting** the converged `(k-1)`-state fit (SMEM-style): empirically **unsafe** — a single split cannot undo the state merging in the smaller fit, so on well-separated 3-state data it reached a *worse* k=3 optimum (−251346 vs random −236009) yet a large gain-over-parent made naive "trust" heuristics accept it; the only safe variant (augment + always take best) is *slower*, not faster. Reverted the scan changes and removed the `split_model` helper; documented the negative result in `scan_states` and [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md). A robust version needs full split+merge SMEM (out of scope). **21 burst_h2mm tests green.**
* **MMFDB — collapsed the auth provider registry to fixed local+ldap dispatch (PRD-59).** No auth providers beyond local + LDAP are planned, so the open extension mechanism was removed: deleted `register_provider`/`build_provider`/`available_providers`/`ProviderContext`/`_PROVIDER_FACTORIES` from `security/auth_providers.py`, and `login.resolve_provider` is again a fixed `local`/`ldap` dispatch (unknown → `AuthError`); the local-always-available fallback now constructs `LocalAuthProvider` directly. The `AuthProvider` protocol + `LocalAuthProvider`/`LdapAuthProvider` remain (the protocol is the seam if a provider is ever needed). Swapped the three registry tests in `test_auth_hardening.py` for a `resolve_provider` dispatch test; updated PRD-59 (removed OIDC/SAML + external-IdP as non-goals → "no further providers planned"), `architecture/mmfdb.md`, and HANDOVER. Standalone **466 passed, 1 skipped**; auth suites green. Advances [PRD-59](/prds/prd-59.md).
* **Burst — H2MM engine: four compounding speedups (E-step fusion, SQUAREM, spectral build, float32).** Second optimisation pass on `core/h2mm.py`, each gated by the A/B-vs-`H2MM_C` tests. (1) **Two-pass E-step:** folded the γ (occupancy) and W (transition) accumulation into the single backward sweep and replaced the `(N, n)` β array with two `(n,)` vectors (β[n] needs only β[n+1]) — halving the large-array memory traffic; ~3–9 % faster (bigger at low `n`). (2) **SQUAREM acceleration** (`optimize(accelerate=True)`, default): squared-extrapolation EM (Varadhan & Roland 2008 S3) with a monotonicity safeguard reaching the *identical* fixed point in far fewer maps — 2-state **81→33** maps (2.4× faster), 3-state **807→132** (6× faster) on well-separated data. (3) **Spectral cache build** (`_build_caches_eig` + `_fill_caches`): for sparse photon streams (`n ≥ 3`, `max Δt ≥ 512`) `A^Δt`/`ρ` come from an eigendecomposition via divided differences instead of binary exponentiation (1.4–2.4× faster build at `max_dt≈2200`), conditioning-guarded with a pair-power fall-back; dense data keeps pair-power. (4) Opt-in **`single_precision`** float32 hot loop + caches (~1.9× at 3 states), explicitly approximate. Also fixed a latent landmine: ChiSurf's `env_bootstrap` rewrites `NUMBA_NUM_THREADS` *after* numba's pool launches, which crashed the first late cold compile (the float32 kernel) via numba's reload guard — `optimize` now re-pins the env to numba's launched pool size (`_sync_numba_threads`). New engine tests (SQUAREM≡plain-EM + fewer maps, eig≡pair-power build, eig declines on defective `A`, float32 near float64); **21 burst_h2mm tests green** (stable across repeated full-dir runs). Net vs `H2MM_C` on the slow benchmark: **0.51×** (2-state) / **0.52×** (3-state) wall-time per map, now also converging in fewer maps. Documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).
* **Burst — H2MM A/B *performance* guard vs `H2MM_C`.** Added `test_benchmark_vs_reference` (2- and 3-state) to `tests/test_ab_vs_h2mm_c.py` as a companion to the correctness A/B tests: it times a full EM run of the numba port against the reference C `H2MM_C` on identical tttrlib-simulated data, reports **ms/EM-iteration** (JIT warmed up first, so compilation isn't charged; normalised per iteration so convergence-count differences don't skew it), and asserts (a) the two engines reach the same optimum and (b) the port stays under ~1.5× the reference time/iter — a wide-margin regression guard that would catch an `O(N·n⁴)`-style slowdown. Marked `slow` (excluded from default runs; run with `-m slow -s`). Measured on 150k-photon dense bursts: **0.68×** (2-state) / **0.50×** (3-state) the `H2MM_C` wall-time per iteration. Documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).
* **Burst — H2MM E-step now beats the reference `H2MM_C` (defer the ρ contraction).** The parallel E-step (`core/h2mm.py::_estep`) formed the transition tensor ξ *per gap* — an `O(N·n⁴)` inner loop that also streamed the whole `rho_cache` from memory once per photon — leaving the numba engine ~1.05–1.21× *slower* than `H2MM_C` (gap widening with `n_states`). Restructured to accumulate only the per-unique-Δt weight `W[slot,k,m] = Σ_gaps α[n,k]·obs[m,y_{n+1}]·β[n+1,m]/c` in the hot loop (`O(N·n²)`, thread-local), then contract `ξ[i,j] = Σ_{slot,k,m} W[slot,k,m]·ρ[slot,k,m,i,j]` **once per slot** in the serial reduction (`O(n_slots·n⁴)`, `n_slots` = unique inter-photon Δt ≪ N). Mathematically identical (ρ is fixed per slot, so the per-gap sum factors out); `rho_cache` is now read `n_slots` times instead of N. On 2000×120-photon simulated data (100 EM iters) the engine went from ~1.05×/0.95×/1.12× the `H2MM_C` wall-time at 2/3/4 states to **0.61×/0.37×/0.28×** — i.e. ~1.6×/2.7×/3.6× *faster*; the 4-state fit dropped 1253→334 ms. All 10 A/B-vs-`H2MM_C` + engine tests still green (converged logL/BIC/params and Viterbi match the reference to the same tolerances). Documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).
* **MMFDB — threaded + enforced `auth` across the whole `api.py` boundary (INC-04).** Most `api.py` functions ran unauthenticated and lacked an `auth` parameter — yet **all ~40 are registered as `mmfdb.v1.*` RPCs invoked via `h(**params, auth=auth)`**, so those versioned methods would have `TypeError`'d the moment they were called with a token: a latent break *and* the enforcement gap. Added `auth` to every one (samples/experiments/operations/parameters/graph/setups/chinet/branches/audit) with shared helpers for **progressive enforcement**: `_acting_user_id` (authenticated principal, else configured default — preserves in-process/GUI), `_new_object_acl` (writes stamp the owner + a default ACL: samples/experiments join the existing artifact/operation ACLs), `_acl_read_or_pass`/`_acl_filter_or_pass` (reads enforce ACLs *where they exist*, stay open otherwise — no legacy lockout), and `_effective_target_user` making the user-scoped branch ops **self-or-admin** (fixed an IDOR where any user could set/read another's active branch). New `tests/test_api_auth.py` (5: auth accepted + owner-ACL + cross-user filtering, graceful no-ACL reads, in-process default-user attribution, IDOR blocked, admin-may-target-other). Standalone **468 passed, 1 skipped** (was 463); `test/fio` **236 passed** (1 pre-existing). Marked [INC-04](/specs/assessment.md#inc-04) 🚧 ADDRESSED. (Landed alongside a concurrent `mmfdb.admin`→`mmfdb_admin` extraction in the tree; committed only the `api.py`/test changes.)
* **Burst — new H2MM photon-by-photon HMM plugin (`burst_h2mm`).** Added a single-molecule FRET plugin that resolves sub-burst state dynamics on the microsecond scale, ported from the Pirchi *et al.* 2016 / `H2MM_C` algorithm into a **self-contained numba engine** (no external H2MM dependency). `core/h2mm.py` caches `A^Δt` and the transition-count `ρ` tensor once per **unique** inter-photon Δt via associative pair-power binary exponentiation (cost scales with photons, not clock ticks), runs a scaled forward-backward + Baum-Welch EM, and provides Viterbi+ICL, BIC, a model factory and a validation simulator. Follows the client-server standard: Qt-free `core/` (h2mm/photons/analysis) → RPC `backend/services.py` (`burst_h2mm.jobs.compute`) → thin `H2mmClient` + `H2mmTool` GUI (FRET states, transition-density plot, BIC/ICL model selection, per-state dwell-time distributions) + click CLI. Consumes `.bur` bursts sliced from `tttrlib.TTTR`, mapping routing-channel + micro-time windows to photon streams. Wired into `burst_analysis` as **step 6 "H2MM"** with workflow-context handoff (inherits burst folder + channel defs). Marked **experimental** (numba engine validated on simulated ground-truth recovery, monotonic logL, BIC selection, Viterbi, RPC, stream-gating, headless GUI). **A/B-verified numerically equivalent to the reference `H2MM_C`** on tttrlib-simulated data carried through the real `tttrlib.TTTR` + plugin extraction path: fixed-model and converged log-likelihood/BIC agree to ~1e-9, π/trans/obs to ~1e-7 (2- and 3-state), and Viterbi paths match 100% over ~36k photons (`tests/test_ab_vs_h2mm_c.py`, skips if `H2MM_C` absent). 15 tests green; not yet validated on experimental data. Documented in [burst plugins](/plugins/burst.md).

* **MMFDB — closed a critical auth hole + enforced "local always available" (PRD-59 security review).** Auditing "what else needs doing," found that an **external (LDAP) user could be logged in via the local provider with an empty password**: JIT-provisioned directory users have no local `password_hash`, and `LocalAuthProvider`'s (and legacy `password_services.login_handler`'s) "no hash → accept when no password" branch treated them as passwordless — `login(provider="local", user_id="<ldap_uid>", password="")` succeeded without the directory. Fixed by making **both** local-auth paths reject users whose `auth_provider != 'local'` (genuine local passwordless users are unaffected). Also found a **lockout risk**: with LDAP as the configured default, the bootstrap **local admin couldn't log in** (default dispatch sent everyone to LDAP). Added a **local fallback** in `login()` — when a non-local default returns `None`, the local provider is tried — making "Local always available" real; it can't weaken security because the local provider now rejects external-homed users (a directory-rejected external user still fails). Third finding: **email-match could hijack a real local account** — an LDAP user whose email collides with an existing local admin was silently relinked (`auth_provider→ldap`), handing control to whoever holds that directory account. Now `resolve_or_provision_user` only email-adopts a **placeholder** local account (local-homed, no password); a real local-credential or other-provider account is never converted (JIT mints a distinct account instead). 4 new regression tests (external-user local-login blocked incl. empty password; local admin logs in under LDAP-default; external user can't sneak through the fallback; email collision doesn't hijack a local password account). Standalone **461 passed, 1 skipped** (was 457); `test/fio` **236 passed** (1 pre-existing).

The nine methods (`get_citations`/`add_citation`/`delete_citation`, `get_product_categories`/`add_product_category`, `get_products`/`add_product`, `get_standards`/`add_standard`) are **dead code** — zero callers anywhere in mmfdb/chisurf/tests, and any call would raise `no such table`. Deleted them (and their two section-comment headers) rather than leave the just-converted-but-unreachable `dao.insert` calls. The still-present `chem_descriptors`/`images`/`flr_photon_stream`/`optical_properties`/`mmfdb_vocabulary`/`flr_experiment_key_value` tables **do** exist, so those conversions stand. Standalone **421 passed, 1 skipped**. Audit: repository.py select 28 → 24, bespoke 1 → 0 (removed the citeulike `IN(...)` read). Advances [PRD-26](/prds/prd-26.md)/[INC-05](/specs/assessment.md#inc-05).

## 2026-07-06
* **MMFDB — god-class breakup: `repository.py` 6,397 → 1,848 lines (−71%).** Resumed and largely completed the Phase-4 [PRD-26](/prds/prd-26.md)/[INC-05](/specs/assessment.md#inc-05) decomposition of the `MFDatabase` god-class into per-concern query mixins under `queries/`. Extracted six new mixins this pass — **ProbeMixin** (probe/spectra/optical/Förster), **SampleMixin** (samples/entities/positions/linkage), **SetupCalibMixin** (setups/calibrations), **ObjectStoreMixin** (object store + materialization), **ArtifactOpsMixin** (the artifact/operation/edge/provenance-graph core, ~46 methods), and **AnalysisMixin** (analysis runs/products/metadata) — for **13 mixins** total. Built a reusable AST-boundary method extractor (handles multi-line signatures, decorators, and leaves class attributes in place); relocated module-level helpers (`_default_reference_spectra_path`→`store/database_resolver`, `_validate_checksum`→`schema/_sqlutil`) to avoid repository↔mixin import cycles, and carried class-level method aliases (`save_setup_snapshot`, `link_operation_artifact`) into their mixins. Public `MFDatabase` surface unchanged (methods resolve via the MRO); standalone suite **419 passed** after every extraction. `repository.py` is now a thin composition over `self.conn`/`self.dao`/`self.lineage` — what remains is the legitimate core (init/connection/properties, migration, audit, vocabulary, experiment key-values, pdbx metadata).
* **MMFDB — admin GUI moved out; `adapters/` subpackage added.** Continued the clean-bounds migration: relocated the chisurf-coupled admin **GUI** (24 modules + 7 view-spec JSONs) out of the package into the ChiSurf plugin (`chisurf/plugins/core/mmfdb_admin/gui/`), replacing the compat wrappers and retargeting 38 importers + the manifest entrypoint; the admin **backend** (RPC handlers) stays in `mmfdb.admin` and is chisurf-free. Added an **`adapters/`** subpackage as the home for external-system bridges — moved `chinet_adapter` → `mmfdb.adapters.chinet` (ChiSurf fit sessions → MMFDB), with eLabFTW / electronic-lab-notebook adapters to follow; adapters keep target-system imports lazy so the core still imports standalone. Top-level `mmfdb` is now 5 files. Standalone: 419 passed. Advances [PRD-24](/prds/prd-24.md)/[PRD-48](/prds/prd-48.md).
* **MMFDB — own hermetic test suite + concern-subpackage reorg (PRD-24).** Gave the package clear bounds and a maintainable file layout. (1) **Relocated ~35 pure-MMFDB test modules** from ChiSurf `test/fio`+`test/plugins` into `modules/mmfdb/tests/` with a hermetic conftest (isolation via MMFDB's own `MMFDB_SETTINGS_DIR`, no chisurf import); the suite runs standalone (`cd modules/mmfdb && PYTHONPATH=src pytest`). This immediately exposed **real boundary violations** in the package — fixed the module-level ones (`admin/backend/services` used `from chisurf import logging` → stdlib; `{measurement,ndxplorer}_services` imported `chisurf.server.services` error helpers → new `mmfdb.admin.backend._service_errors`). ChiSurf↔MMFDB integration tests (admin GUI `MMFDBClient`, chinet/`parameter_registry` alignment, ndxplorer submodule, chisurf test-data) stay in the ChiSurf tree. (2) **Reorganized the 38 flat top-level modules into concern subpackages** — `schema/ store/ provenance/ samples/ lifecycle/ security/ project/` — leaving 6 core files at top (`repository`, `api`, `models`, `config`, `chinet_adapter`, `__init__`); collapsed the `auth/`-only-`__init__` "package" to `auth.py`. Hard cutover (no compat shims): every internal, test, and ChiSurf import retargeted to grouped paths (`mmfdb.schema.dao`, `mmfdb.provenance.result_registry`, …); fixed `Path(__file__).parent/"data"` resolution in the seven moved modules that read bundled data. **Proof of clean bounds: 419 passed with only `src` on the path** (no chisurf, no chinet). * **Amplitude scale-invariance: diagnosed, deliberately not "fixed"**: `Lifetime.amplitudes` normalises by `|a|/sum|a|` *and* the decay is autoscaled to the data (`rescale_w_bg`, enabled by fixing `n0`), so the amplitude scale is redundant twice over — n parameters, n-1 degrees of freedom. Measured directly: at equal starting amplitudes the `xL1`/`xL2` Jacobian columns are exact mirror images (|J| 398/398, 102/102, 340/340; cos = -1), the amplitude block is numerically rank 1 with the lifetime block full rank as a control, and scaling every amplitude by 3.7x leaves the model bit-identical. Overall Jacobian condition number ~1e10.
  **The obvious fix does not work, and the measurement says so.** Pinning one amplitude to remove the null direction was tested across 24 randomised starts: parameter recovery was **16/24 in both arms** — identical. It moves median chi2r 2.98 -> 1.01 (the nuisance parameters `sc`/`bg` converge better once conditioning improves; chi2r 2.98 was repeatedly observed alongside *correct* lifetimes 1.200/4.009) at ~24% more fit time, but the lifetimes are unaffected. An initial 6-start probe suggested a much larger effect and was overturned by the sweep — recorded here so the anecdote is not re-run as if it were evidence. The parameterisation is therefore left unchanged and the behaviour is pinned by `test/fitting/test_amplitude_degeneracy.py` (4 tests) instead.
  A second, distinct defect surfaced: with equal amplitudes *and* close lifetimes the fit stalls completely (only `sc` moves; `bg`/amplitudes/lifetimes frozen at their starts) — an exchange-symmetry saddle, not the scale invariance. The control case, close lifetimes with *unequal* amplitudes (0.7/0.3), converges to chi2r 3.26 where equal amplitudes give 166.6.
  Suites in isolation: 4 + 7(+1 xfail) + 10 + 17 + 13 + 9 = 60 passed. Note `test/fitting/` cannot currently be collected as a whole — `test_anisotropy_integrals.py` raises `FileNotFoundError` at collection and the combined run aborts with a fatal error; both reproduce with the new file excluded and are pre-existing.

* **`shift_array` was discontinuous and off by one — the reason fits plateaued at chi2r ~3**: Two bugs in `chisurf/core/math/signal.py`, both hitting the `timeshift` fit parameter.
  (1) *Off-by-one for fractional negative shifts.* `ts_i = int(ts)` truncates toward zero while `ts_f` used `floor()`, so below zero they disagreed: `-1.5` shifted by `-0.5`, and `-0.25` produced a **right** shift with wrapped data at index 0. Integer shifts were correct, which hid it — and the existing tests encoded the wrong values, so they had to be corrected rather than merely re-run.
  (2) *A jump discontinuity at every integer shift.* The out-of-range region was blanked via `ceil()`/`floor()`, so an infinitesimal shift zeroed an entire channel. Measured finite-difference slope diverged as `1/h`: 1e9 at h=1e-9, 1e6 at h=1e-6. Fixed by replacing only the out-of-range sample's *share* at the partial boundary channel, so the result is continuous; the implied slope is now bounded (~7) and jumps scale linearly with h.
  **(2) is why `timeshift` never moved.** It is a fit parameter starting at 0, and the fabricated slope made its Jacobian column ~1000x every other column (1.8e5 vs ~200 for the lifetimes); LM proposed a large step, it did not help, and `ts` stayed pinned at exactly 0. Profiling 24 randomised starts by cluster made this unambiguous: every fit reaching chi2r ~1 had moved `ts` off zero, every fit stuck on the chi2r ~3 plateau had `ts` = 0.0000 with otherwise *correct* lifetimes (1.200/4.009).
  **Result**: fits reaching chi2r < 1.1 went 11/24 -> 15/24 at the shipped optimiser settings, and the chi2r ~3 plateau disappeared entirely (every fit now lands at ~1.0 or clearly diverges). This also explains the chaotic behaviour seen while investigating the amplitude parameterisation — the 0.98-converges/0.90-stalls pattern and the 405-vs-230 evaluation swings were a noise-driven Jacobian, not the parameterisation.
  Verified against an independent `v[k - shift]` reference (exact, atol 1e-12) across 13 shifts and both `outside_value` settings. Suites: 4 + 7(+1 xfail) + 10 + 17 + 9 + 37 + 24 + 1 = 109 passed. Pre-existing and unrelated: `test/math/test_interp.py` and `test_interpolate_shift_empty.py` fail to collect (missing `burst_mle_analysis` plugin) and `test_datatools.py::test_distance_between_gaussian` fails — all three reproduce with the change stashed.
  **Still open**: the optimiser's `epsfcn: 0` default makes MINPACK use machine epsilon, a step below the model's numerical noise floor. With the shift fix in place, `epsfcn=1e-4` reaches 23/24 valid vs 15/24 for the default. Not changed here — it is a global default affecting every fit and is so far validated only on one two-exponential fixture.

* **GUI fit crashed with SIGABRT — a heap overrun in the periodic-convolution call**: `convolve_lifetime_spectrum_periodic` passed `stop`/`conv_stop` straight through to `tttrlib.fconv_per_cs`. Callers supply `n_points`, a *length*, while `fconv_per_cs` treats those arguments as inclusive *indices*, so the call touched one element past the end of `decay` and `irf`. Fixed by clamping both to `min(len(irf), len(decay), n_points) - 1`, matching the numba twin `convolve_lifetime_spectrum_periodic_nb`, which has always clamped — the guard was lost when the tttrlib path was switched in.
  **This was self-inflicted and the dev environment hid it.** The switch to `fconv_per_cs` was made against a locally rebuilt tttrlib whose SWIG wrapper clamps internally (`conv_stop = n_irf - 1`); the released tttrlib 0.27.0 in the canonical pixi env does not, so every fit in the GUI aborted. Measured directly on the stock build: `conv_stop = n` -> exit 134, `conv_stop = n - 1` and `n/2` -> clean, 200 repetitions clean. Classic overrun behaviour — the abort had no message and its traceback pointed at an unrelated `tobytes()` in the IRF cache, simply because that was the next allocation.
  Reproduced headlessly in the pixi env (exit 134), confirmed **not** caused by the `shift_array` change by A/B-ing that commit (crash present either way), then fixed and re-verified (exit 0, six fits complete). Regression coverage in `test/test_periodic_convolution_bounds.py` (9 tests) pins the clamp; note it only discriminates on a non-clamping tttrlib, so it was additionally verified by hand in the pixi env — passes with the fix, `AssertionError: conv_stop==n not clamped to n-1` without it.
  **Lesson: prefer fixing the caller.** The earlier tttrlib-side SWIG clamp was the right hardening but the wrong sole remedy — it made ChiSurf depend on an unreleased patch. The bounds contract now holds against any tttrlib build.
  Suites (arm64): 9 + 9 + 7(+1 xfail) + 4 + 37 + 24 + 1 = 91 passed.

* **GUI: compiled-`.ui` cache in `init_with_ui`**: `uic.loadUi` re-parses the `.ui` XML on *every* widget construction. `chisurf/gui/decorators.py` now compiles each file once (`uic.compileUi` + `exec`), caches the generated `Ui_*` class keyed on (path, mtime), and calls its `setupUi`. Per-construction cost across the 41 loadable `.ui` files in the tree: **3.40 ms -> 0.52 ms**. End to end, `LinePlot` went **~20.9 -> ~19.2 ms (8%)**, measured as the median of 10 constructions in three *separate* processes.
  **The trap, which I hit:** `pyuic5`'s `setupUi` parents the widgets to the target but binds them as attributes of the **Ui_ instance** (`self.lineEdit`), whereas `loadUi(path, target)` binds them on the *target*. The first version swapped one for the other directly — the widget tree was identical and every `self.<widget>` in widget code would have raised `AttributeError`. Caught by sweeping all 53 `.ui` files and comparing child names *and* bound attributes: 41 identical, 0 different, 7 fall back (do not compile), 5 that `loadUi` cannot load either. Covered by `test/gui/test_ui_compile_cache.py` (45 passed, 12 skipped), including mtime invalidation and graceful fallback for missing/malformed files.
  **Honest trade-off:** compiling costs about as much as one `loadUi` (3.51 vs 3.40 ms), so break-even is **1.22 constructions per file**. A widget built exactly once is ~0.63 ms slower; anything built twice or more wins. Plots are rebuilt per fit, so they win; once-only dialogs pay a little. Precompiling with `pyuic5` at build time would remove the one-time cost entirely and is the better long-term answer.
  **Not pursued:** `LinePlot`'s three `PlotWidget`s (the dominant remaining cost) cannot be created lazily — all three are simultaneously visible in a `DockArea` (Residuals / A.corr. residuals / Data), not tabbed.
  **Method note:** cProfile again over-attributed — it credited `load_ui` 6.4 ms of a 21 ms `LinePlot`, while direct timing showed 1.84 ms. And an in-process `git stash` A/B gave a corrupted comparison (a stale `PlotWidget` C++ object); the reliable measurement was separate processes.
  Suites: 45(+12 skipped) + 3 + 4 + 9 + 7(+1 xfail) + 37 = 105 passed.

* **"The plot does not update reliably" — a missing `editingFinished` in `ScientificDoubleSpinBox`**: `ScientificDoubleSpinBox` subclasses `QAbstractSpinBox` and manages its own value, connecting the **inner QLineEdit's** `editingFinished` to its text commit. That is a *different signal object* from the spin box's own `editingFinished`, and `QAbstractSpinBox` does not forward it for such a subclass. Every `FittingParameterWidget` connects to the spin box's `editingFinished` — `parameter_widgets.py` contains **zero** `valueChanged`/`sigValueChanged` connections — so committing typed text updated the display and emitted `sigValueChanged` but never reached the model.
  **Why it looked intermittent rather than broken**: stepping with the arrows worked, because `stepBy()` emits `editingFinished` explicitly; typing a value and pressing Enter (the common interaction) left the model, the fit and the plots on the old number. Measured on all three paths before the fix — arrows: propagated; typing+Enter: **not propagated**; programmatic `setValue`: not propagated. The last is deliberate and kept: that is how fit results are pushed back into the widgets, and emitting there would write the value straight back into the model.
  Fixed by re-emitting `self.editingFinished` in `_commit_text`, correcting a comment that asserted the opposite. Covered by `test/gui/test_spinbox_editing_finished.py` (9 tests, incl. two end-to-end asserting the `FittingParameter` follows the widget); verified to discriminate — **3 failed without the fix, 9 pass with it**.
  **Measured widget overhead (no change made)**: `FittingParameterWidget` costs **0.43–0.50 ms** each, against 0.035 ms for its spin box and 0.046 ms for the `FittingParameter` — the remainder is `_build_layout` (0.16 ms, 31%), three spin boxes (0.13 ms, 25%) and general Qt construction, with nothing pathological to remove. It matters at scale: a 128-exponential FRET model has ~256 parameters, i.e. **~128 ms** of widget construction. The lever there is virtualizing the parameter panel (not building widgets for off-screen parameters), which is a substantially larger change and is not attempted here.
  Suites: 9 + 45(+12 skipped) + 3 + 4 + 11 + 9 + 7(+1 xfail) = 88 passed.

* **Prior settings moved inline into the parameter popup**: the per-parameter popup showed a prior radio row, a `repr()` summary and an **Edit...** button that opened a *second* modal (`PriorEditorDialog`, "Advanced prior settings") just to set mu/sigma. The distribution selector and its parameter spin boxes are now built directly into `FittingParameterDetailPopup`: choosing a family from a `Distribution:` combo rebuilds the parameter form in place, and editing a spin box applies the prior immediately — no OK button, no second window. `PriorEditorDialog` is **removed** (91 lines) rather than deprecated.
  Families with no editable parameter list (`CallablePrior`, `ProductPrior`) fall back to a read-only summary label instead of pretending to be editable. The quick radios (Box / Gaussian / Log-normal / Custom) are kept as one-click shortcuts; "Custom" now just reveals the full family list rather than launching a dialog. Minor redundancy noted and left: with Gaussian selected both the radio and the combo read "Gaussian".
  The two tests covering the deleted dialog were **ported, not dropped** — `test/gui/test_parameter_prior_widget.py` now asserts the inline behaviour (spin boxes appear, edits apply without an OK, switching family in the combo applies it, the editor hides for Box, an existing prior populates the form, and an uneditable prior degrades to a summary). Verified visually with offscreen `QWidget.grab()` renders for the box/Gaussian/Gamma states.
  Suites: 14 + 9 + 45(+12 skipped) + 3 + 4 + 11 = 86 passed.

* **Amplitude parameterisation fixed: one amplitude per `Lifetime` is held out of the optimiser**. Amplitudes are normalised by `|a|/sum|a|`, so scaling them all is a no-op — n parameters, n-1 degrees of freedom. `Lifetime._update_redundant_amplitude()` now marks the first free amplitude `redundant` whenever normalisation is on and no amplitude already pins the scale; `FittingParameterGroup.parameters` excludes redundant parameters alongside fixed and linked ones.
  **`redundant` is a new concept, deliberately not `fixed`.** `Lifetime.update()` writes the normalised values back into the parameters, and a `fixed` parameter *ignores writes* — marking it fixed would make the stored amplitudes drift away from the normalised ones on every update. A redundant parameter is still written; it is simply not varied. Idempotence of `update()` is pinned by a test.
  **Result** (two-exponential fixture): `cond(J)` **5.49e7 -> 554**, amplitude uncertainty **4,801,893% -> 1.8%**, with chi2r (1.014 -> 1.017), the lifetimes (4.0089/1.2007 -> 4.0089/1.2003) and the amplitude ratio (0.694384 -> 0.693764) all unchanged. The fitted answer is the same; only its uncertainty becomes meaningful.
  **Held-out amplitudes still report an uncertainty**: `Fit._propagate_redundant_error_estimates` derives it from the sum-to-one constraint as `sqrt(sum of the siblings' covariance block)`, off-diagonal terms included — they dominate, because the fractions are strongly anti-correlated. Verified exact for n=2, where sigma(x1) must equal sigma(x2): both 0.00792584. Without this the held-out parameter would keep a *stale* estimate from an earlier fit, which is worse than none.
  Edge cases covered: a single component holds out its only amplitude (its normalised value is always 1, so it carries no freedom at all); an amplitude the user already fixed pins the scale and nothing is held out; three components keep two degrees of freedom; disabling `normalize_amplitudes` frees all of them; `pop()` clears the flag on the detached parameter and reassigns.
  **This supersedes the earlier "measured, deliberately not fixed" entry.** That assessment scored the degeneracy by parameter recovery (16/24 either way) and chi2r, found no difference, and concluded it was not worth fixing — the wrong metric. The degeneracy does not harm convergence, it destroys the *error estimates*, which is what gets published; the user's own fit showed `xL1 +-62.4%` / `xL2 +-62.1%`. `test/fitting/test_amplitude_degeneracy.py` is retired into `test/fitting/test_amplitude_redundancy.py` (13 tests), keeping the two tests that document *why* the hold-out is needed.
  Regressions: 13 + 7(+1 xfail) + 10 + 17 + 9 + 9 + 14 + 9 + 37 = 125 passed. Pre-existing and unrelated failures (identical with the change stashed): `test_fret_line.py` 6, `test_user_models.py` 2, `test_forbidden_communication.py` 3.

* **Optimiser `epsfcn` default: machine epsilon -> 1e-6**: MINPACK derives its forward-difference step as `sqrt(epsfcn) * |x|`, and `epsfcn: 0` means "use machine epsilon" — a step of ~1.5e-8 relative. That is far below the noise floor of the decay model, whose convolution is recursive over ~1024 channels, so the Jacobian columns came back dominated by rounding noise and the optimiser could fail to move the lifetimes **at all** (they stayed at *exactly* their starting values while only the nuisance parameters moved).
  Re-measured from scratch after the `shift_array` and amplitude fixes, since both changed the landscape — the earlier numbers recommending 1e-4 were stale, and with better conditioning a much smaller step now suffices. Over **88 randomised fits across four independent conditions** (three start seeds, a different noise realisation, and a 3-exponential model), fits reaching chi2r < 1.1: `epsfcn=0` **60/88**, 1e-10 81/88, 1e-8 82/88, **1e-6 83/88**. 1e-6 was no worse than any alternative in any single condition, for roughly 10-30% more time; 1e-2 regressed (18/24), so the improvement is not monotonic in step size.
  **The bundled default alone would have been inert.** `copy_settings_to_user_folder` uses `if not destination_file.exists()`, so user settings are copied to `~/.chisurf` once and **never refreshed** — every existing install carries the old `epsfcn: 0`, which is exactly the broken value. `Fit._leastsq_options()` therefore treats 0 (MINPACK's "pick for me") as unset and substitutes `DEFAULT_EPSFCN`; explicit non-zero values pass through, so a machine-epsilon step stays reachable by asking for it. Verified through the real `fit.run()` path with `epsfcn: 0` still on disk: **16/24 -> 23/24 valid**.
  **Bonus: this also fixed the at-the-bound defect** tracked as a strict xfail (`test_fit_does_not_destroy_a_good_solution`). A parameter sitting exactly on a bound has zero derivative under the sin/arcsin transform, and `scatter` defaults to 0.0 with bounds (0.0, 100.0) — exactly there; starting at the optimum drove it 0 -> 7.8 and chi2r 1.55 -> 1765. With a ~1.5e-8 probe the difference quotient never left the flat region, so the derivative really was zero; at a 1e-3 relative step it reaches far enough to see the real slope. The xfail is retired (now `8 passed`), with the explanation kept as a comment. No change to the bound handling was needed.
  Covered by `test/fitting/test_leastsq_epsfcn_default.py` (8 tests: zero treated as unset, missing key filled, explicit values honoured, garbage tolerated, other options untouched, the global settings dict not mutated, and end-to-end that the lifetimes actually move from a start that previously froze).
  Suites: 8 + 8 + 13 + 2 + 3 + 8 + 9 + 3 = 54 passed, plus 71 (`test_fitting_client`), 9 (`test_decay_fit`), 14 (`test_fret_species_decay`), 13 (`test_view_spec`), 17, 10, 9 — all green.
